providers.description: Legacy is a United States direct-to-consumer male fertility company offering at-home sperm testing and sperm cryopreservation without a clinic visit. Customers order a collection kit online, provide a sample at home, and return it by free overnight shipping to Legacy's CLIA-certified, CLEP-approved laboratory, where results appear in a private client dashboard within 48 hours of receipt. Services span basic, standard, and advanced semen analysis (count, concentration, motility, morphology, and Halosperm sperm DNA fragmentation), STI testing, multi-year sperm storage bundles, and male fertility supplements. Legacy serves people trying to conceive and those preserving fertility ahead of a vasectomy, testosterone therapy, gender-affirming care, cancer treatment, or military deployment, and is in-network with selected insurers and employer fertility benefit programs. Legacy publishes no public developer API; its notable machine-readable surface is a first-party llms.txt written for AI answer engines.

providers.name: Pathai
providers.description: PathAI is a healthcare artificial-intelligence company transforming pathology through machine learning. Its AISight Image Management System (IMS) and the AISight Link open API deliver AI-assisted disease detection, biomarker quantification, fields-of-interest and AI Impressions, and laboratory workflow integration for pathologists, hospital and reference labs, and biopharma research partners. AISight Link is an enterprise interoperability surface that connects AISight with third-party AI algorithms and Laboratory Information Systems (LIS/LIMS) over REST and HL7; PathAI does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs. The company is ISO 27001 certified and operates a vulnerability disclosure program. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 8vc.

providers.name: TrueCoach
providers.description: TrueCoach is a personal-training and remote-coaching platform for strength coaches, personal trainers, and physical therapists to deliver workouts online and train clients remotely. Started as Fitbot out of Techstars Boulder and now an Xplor Technologies brand, it offers a web app plus iOS and Android client apps with program and workout builders, a video exercise library, nutrition tracking, wearables data, Stripe-powered payments, a MyFitnessPal integration, and a Zapier connector — but publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Vergent Bioscience
providers.description: Vergent Bioscience is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, developing tumor-targeted fluorescent imaging agents for real-time intraoperative tumor visualization. Its lead compound, abenacianine for injection (VGT-309), is designed to let surgeons see previously undetected or difficult-to-find tumors during minimally invasive and robotic-assisted cancer surgery so that all tumor tissue can be removed in a single procedure. The company is first evaluating VGT-309 in lung cancer with the stated intent to expand into a wide range of solid tumors. Vergent publishes no developer program, no REST or GraphQL API, and no SDKs — it is a therapeutics and imaging-agent developer, not a software vendor. The only machine-readable surfaces on its own domain are a Wix-platform-generated llms.txt and a live, anonymous Model Context Protocol endpoint at /_api/mcp that exposes nine site-content and Wix-platform tools.

providers.name: wiastandards-com
providers.description: WIA Standards (World Certification Industry Association) is a global organization dedicated to developing, maintaining, and promoting certification standards across various industries. With 18 years of experience, it offers over 730 standards covering data exchange, API protocols, digital twins, and interoperability, supporting 24 categories and hundreds of simulators to foster universal compliance and innovation.

providers.name: AdmitBase
providers.description: AdmitBase is a professional-school admissions data platform. It compares an applicant's GPA and standardised test score against the admitted‑student figures each school itself published, and returns a 0‑100 match score classified as Safety, Target, Reach or Far Reach. See your real chances at every law, medical, and dental school — your GPA and test score against admitted‑student data from official disclosures.

providers.name: Airwave
providers.description: Airwave (Indianapolis, founded 2022) is a field intelligence platform for industrial and field-service technicians: ANSI Z87+ smart safety glasses with a built-in camera, microphone and speakers record the job, and the Airwave software turns the footage into inspection reports, job hazard analyses, customer summaries and searchable job notes, with an AI assistant ("Blue") answering questions from uploaded manuals, parts lists and team knowledge. The pricing page lists API integrations (ERP, CRM, CMMS) and an Airwave Glasses SDK only in the custom-priced Video Intelligence tier behind a sales conversation; no public developer documentation, API reference or machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: CoachClub
providers.description: CoachClub — branded "CoachClub by Move Your Fit" — is a French direct-to-consumer online sport and wellness coaching service founded in 2010 in France by Leslie Vartabedian and backed by Serena. Subscribers answer a questionnaire covering goals, physical ability, health and availability, and receive a tailored training and nutrition programme drawn from a library of more than 1,100 on-demand coaching videos spanning over 30 disciplines — fitness, musculation, yoga, danse, cardio boxe, pilates, stretching, bien-être and prénatal/postnatal — graded across three difficulty levels and paired with twelve weeks of healthy recipes, accessible 24/7 from computer, tablet, smartphone or television. The public marketing site runs on WordPress and the member application is a hosted Kajabi tenant at mon.coachclub.com. CoachClub sells an end-user subscription only: it publishes no public API, SDK, webhook catalog, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: TimeSolv
providers.description: TimeSolv provides cloud‑based time tracking, billing, and practice management software for law firms and professional services. Its platform automates billable hour capture, invoicing, trust accounting, client portal, and integrates with QuickBooks, Xero, NetDocuments, Dropbox, LawPay and AI tools. TimeSolv aims to improve efficiency, compliance, and revenue visibility for legal practices.

providers.name: Vida Health
providers.description: Vida Health is a San Francisco-based virtual care company founded in 2014 that combines an AI-powered mobile app with a national network of licensed clinicians, coaches and therapists to prevent, manage and reverse chronic cardiometabolic and behavioral health conditions including obesity, diabetes, hypertension, depression and anxiety. Vida sells a turnkey enterprise programme to employers and health plans, layering GLP-1 prescribing and clinical oversight on top of behavioral coaching, and its platform ingests real-time readings from more than 100 connected devices and consumer health apps to feed outcome reporting back to its enterprise buyers. Vida publishes no public developer portal or API documentation: the API host api.vida.com is live but returns 401 on every path, and data/EHR integration for health plans and employers is arranged through enterprise sales rather than self-service onboarding.

providers.name: DERATE
providers.description: DERATE provides a mobile app that scans truck dashboard or scanner codes (SPN/FMI) to instantly diagnose faults, estimate repair costs, and generate work orders. Available on iOS and upcoming on Android, it targets drivers, operators, and owner‑operators seeking quick, accurate fault code interpretation without specialized equipment. The service offers free usage with optional paid plans for advanced features.

providers.name: Eden Health
providers.description: Eden Health was a primary and virtual care company that delivered app-based medical care, behavioral health, and care navigation to employers and their employees, integrating with health systems and insurers (backed by Insight Partners). It was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public marketing site is no longer reachable over TLS, but its primary backend service — the "Grdn" (Guardian) API at api.edenhealth.com — still serves a Swagger 2.0 description covering patients, appointments, membership, documents, care teams, and clinician tooling.

providers.name: The Clinician
providers.description: The Clinician is a New Zealand-headquartered digital health company whose product, The Clinician Platform (TCP, formerly ZEDOC), is an outcomes-intelligence layer for value-based healthcare. TCP captures patient-reported outcome and experience measures (PROMs, PREMs, CROMs) omnichannel over SMS, email, web and native mobile in 20+ languages, scores and benchmarks them automatically against MCID thresholds, runs configurable digital care pathways with a threshold-triggered alert engine, and returns outcomes to the EMR via FHIR. It sits alongside an EMR/PAS rather than replacing it, and the company markets an API-driven architecture aligned with HL7 FHIR (incl. SMART-on-FHIR), HL7 v2.x, openEHR and DICOM, plus an OMOP Clinical Events API. No public API reference, developer portal or machine-readable contract is published — API access runs through an enterprise sales engagement.

providers.name: Altro Health
providers.description: Altro Health provides a digital health platform that connects patients, providers, and payers to streamline care coordination, telehealth visits, and health data analytics. Founded by a collective of healthcare innovators, the company focuses on improving outcomes through integrated technology solutions and secure data exchange across the healthcare ecosystem.

providers.name: Cardiosense
providers.description: Cardiosense, Inc. is a Chicago-based medical technology company developing AI-powered, noninvasive cardiac hemodynamic monitoring for heart failure care. Its CardioTag device is a wearable chest biosensor that captures seismocardiographic (SCG), electrocardiographic (ECG) and photoplethysmographic (PPG) signals, and its PCWP Analysis Software is a standalone AI software-as-a-medical-device that estimates Pulmonary Capillary Wedge Pressure from those signals without right heart catheterization or an implantable sensor. Both are authorized by the FDA as Class II medical devices, and the company received an FDA De Novo classification. Cardiosense publishes no developer program, SDK or API specification; its only machine-readable surfaces are an authored llms.txt, an extended AI-context document, an explicit AI-crawler allowance in robots.txt, and an OAuth-protected Model Context Protocol server on its own host.

providers.name: Medeloop
providers.description: Medeloop is an AI platform for the clinical research lifecycle, describing itself as an operating system for clinical research that spans grant discovery and funding, real-world evidence generation from patient data, and delivering actionable intelligence at the point of care. Its products include Medeloop Analytics (AI agents that analyze EHR, claims, and registry data without requiring users to code), EvidenceKit (analytics paired with all-payer claims data), Medeloop Grants (AI-assisted grant discovery and proposal writing), and Medeloop Care (population health and care management). The platform is federated (compute moves to the data, which stays in the customer's infrastructure), CDM-agnostic (Epic, Cerner, Meditech, OMOP, i2b2, or custom schemas), and model-agnostic (routing tasks across OpenAI, Anthropic, or DeepSeek), with multi-cloud deployment across AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-premise. It serves pharmaceutical and life-sciences companies, health systems, and clinical researchers. As of this enrichment pass Medeloop publishes no public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification; its documentation host (docs.medeloop.ai) is gated behind Okta authentication and its analytics application is a private client login.

providers.name: Owletcare
providers.description: Owlet (Owletcare) is a baby-monitoring technology company that builds connected-nursery hardware and companion apps for parents. Its flagship Dream Sock is marketed as an FDA-cleared smart baby monitor that tracks a sleeping infant's pulse rate, oxygen levels, movement and sleep patterns, alongside the Dream Sight HD video monitor and the combined Dream Duo system. Products pair a wearable/camera with the Owlet Dream mobile app for real-time wellness insights and notifications. The consumer storefront at owletcare.com runs on Shopify; sign-in is handled by Shopify's Customer Account API (OIDC/OAuth), and Owlet does not currently publish a first-party developer API program. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from Owlet's public web surface.

providers.name: PreciseDx
providers.description: PreciseDx is a New York-based AI digital pathology and oncology diagnostics company, founded out of the digital pathology program at Mount Sinai Health System. Its OncoIntelligence platform applies a patented Morphology Feature Array to hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained tissue images, combining AI-derived morphology features with clinicopathologic factors to produce an OncoIntelligence Score. The flagship test, PreciseBreast, stratifies early-stage breast cancer patients into high- and low-risk cohorts for disease recurrence up to 8.8 years, clinically validated across more than 1,600 cases, returning results in hours rather than the two to six weeks required for gene expression testing and at roughly 30 percent of the cost. PreciseDx operates CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited laboratories in New York City and Miami and is licensed in all 50 states. Test ordering for clinicians is handled through an authenticated web portal; the company publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Aidaly
providers.description: Aidaly is a Miami, Florida home care company, founded in 2021 by CEO Margaret "Maggie" Norris, that trains, employs and pays family members as professional caregivers so households can draw on Medicaid, Medicare and private benefit dollars for care they were already giving unpaid. It runs a software-enabled care agency on its own aidalyOS platform - Aidaly Care, a caregiver mobile app with insurance-required electronic visit verification, care plans, visit notes and pay tracking; AidalyHQ, a credentialed console for supervising nurses; a Learning Studio training library; and a care-team nurse network. It operates in South Florida, Arizona and Michigan with Colorado and Massachusetts announced, is contracted into payer networks including Molina Healthcare and Meridian, displays Vanta-attested SOC 2 and HIPAA badges, and raised $8.5M led by Seven Seven Six. Aidaly publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Koda Health
providers.description: Koda Health is a Houston-based digital health company whose AI-enhanced patient decision support platform digitizes serious illness planning for health systems, health plans, and value-based care organizations. Its two solutions — Advance Care Planning (ACP) and Kidney Action Planning (KAP) for chronic kidney disease — walk patients through video-guided, interactive goals-of-care conversations and produce legally compliant advance directives, medical power of attorney, and POLST/DNR documents with digital signing and notarization across all 50 states. Completed plans are pushed into the provider's EMR through an integration Koda states meets HL7 FHIR standards, and can be shared with care teams, payors, and family. KodaCares adds human Patient Advocates for complex cases. Koda publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; its API host (api.kodahealthcare.com) is a closed backend serving the app, and EMR interoperability is delivered through partner and health-system integrations rather than a self-serve public API.

providers.name: RealWear
providers.description: RealWear builds rugged, hands-free head-mounted and assisted-reality wearable computers (the Navigator series and HMT-1) for frontline and industrial workers in energy, manufacturing, field service, and utilities. Its Android-based devices are operated entirely by voice through the on-device WearHF service, which turns any Android app's touch controls into voice commands and can be tuned with WearML voice directives placed in UI metadata — so there is no separate SDK to install. RealWear now also ships Ari, a voice-first AI assistant (Ari OS and the Ari Cloud dashboard) with Microsoft connectors (Teams, Outlook email and calendar, contacts, Copilot), skills, and cross-session memory. Developers extend the platform with native Android, Unity, React Native, Cordova, Xamarin, and HTML apps plus custom Ari skills. This profile was surfaced as a Foundry Group portfolio company and enriched from RealWear's public developer surface.

providers.name: Telepatia AI
providers.description: Telepatia is an AI-native clinical platform built for Latin American healthcare. It listens to doctor-patient consultations and generates clinical documentation in real time (AI Writer), surfaces evidence-based clinical recommendations during the visit (AI Advisor), integrates with 50+ electronic health record and hospital systems such as Epic, TASY, iClinic and MV (AI Integrator), and produces analytics on protocol adherence and clinical performance (AI Business Intelligence). Founded by Nicolas Abad and backed by a16z with a $33M Series A, the platform has deployed across 25+ hospital systems in Brazil, Colombia and Mexico. As of this enrichment pass Telepatia exposes a product and web application but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: ACTO
providers.description: ACTO is a Toronto-headquartered Life Sciences software company whose Intelligent Field Excellence (IFE) platform prepares biopharmaceutical, biotech and medtech commercial and medical field teams for healthcare-provider conversations. The platform is organized into three product pillars — Educate (learning, certification and MLR-approved content delivery), Engage (coaching, AI roleplay and practice through capabilities such as TalkTRx, CXZone, Journeys and the OmniSight dashboard) and Augment (real-time in-field support, including the LAICA assistant and role-based "SuperAgent" AI) — and is sold to enterprise Life Sciences organizations rather than to developers. ACTO states it supports more than 50,000 field professionals across 100+ countries and is a Veeva Gold Product Partner with validated integrations into Veeva Vault CRM, PromoMats and MedComms, plus an ACTOverse partner marketplace of pre-vetted content, data and services vendors. It is a validated platform compliant with FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and publishes SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001 and GDPR posture through a SafeBase trust center. ACTO publishes no public developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract of any kind — its integration surface is delivered as certified, partner-side work against Veeva's APIs rather than as a first-party public API.

providers.name: Elixir Medical
providers.description: Elixir Medical Corporation is a privately held medical device company headquartered in Milpitas, California, developing implant and interventional platforms for coronary and peripheral artery disease. Its DynamX sirolimus-eluting coronary bioadaptor is designed to restore vessel pulsatility and compliance rather than permanently cage the artery, and holds a European CE mark, Japanese PMDA approval and a U.S. FDA Breakthrough Device designation; the LithiX Hertz Contact intravascular lithotripsy system and the DESyne family of drug-eluting stents round out the portfolio. Elixir Medical operates no developer program and publishes no product, device or clinical API. The only machine-readable surface it serves is the default WordPress REST API of its corporate marketing site, alongside an SEO-plugin-generated llms.txt.

providers.name: Headway
providers.description: Headway operates a national mental-health care platform that connects patients, therapists and psychiatrists, and insurance companies. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in New York, Headway builds the first asset-free national network of behavioral-health providers who accept insurance, handling insurance credentialing, claims management, payments, and scheduling for clinicians while letting patients search for in-network providers, book appointments online, and see costs up front. The company partners with 45+ major insurers (Aetna, Anthem, Cigna, Oxford, UnitedHealthcare, Oscar) and, as of 2026, powers 600,000+ appointments per month across all 50 states. Headway is backed by a16z, Thrive, Accel, GV, Spark Capital, and Forerunner. It maintains SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance. Headway does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Proximie
providers.description: Proximie is a health-tech company building a cloud platform it describes as the operating system for intelligent operating rooms, connecting surgical teams, medical devices, and data for remote telementoring, telesurgery, session recording, and AI-powered surgical insights across 500+ facilities in 50 countries. For developers, Proximie ships a pre-release C++ SDK (media streaming and session management, with an internal REST layer) and runs a Development Partners program that lets OEMs and medtech companies embed real-time connectivity, secure data routing, and white-label collaboration into their own devices. Proximie also open-sources WebRTC/Janus tooling (jarust, janus-mobile-sdk). Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: Sempre Health
providers.description: Sempre Health is a San Francisco based digital health company, founded in 2015, that operates a behavior-based dynamic pricing platform for prescription medications. Working with health plans, pharmacy benefit managers and pharmaceutical manufacturers, it enrolls covered members and adjusts their copay at the point of fill through SMS outreach: the more consistently a member refills on time, the deeper the discount. The company reports more than 19 payer and PBM partners covering roughly 60% of commercially insured lives in the United States, availability at retail pharmacies in all 50 states, and HITRUST certification alongside a signed BAA with each plan. As of this profile Sempre Health publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract; its own health-plans page describes payer integration as sharing a list of eligible members rather than as an API.

providers.name: Sworkit
providers.description: Sworkit Health is a digital wellbeing platform combining on-demand fitness, mindfulness, mobility and recovery, nutrition, and wellness challenges to help organizations improve employee engagement and workforce health. Rather than a public REST API, Sworkit exposes its workout content to developers through the Sworkit Workout Player Platform — an embeddable web player and a React Native mobile SDK component, both published on npm under the @sworkit org. Its security and compliance posture covers SOC 2 Type 2, HIPAA, and GDPR.

providers.name: Ellipsis Health
providers.description: Ellipsis Health is a healthcare AI company that has established the human voice as a vital sign for mental health, using clinically validated vocal-biomarker technology, natural language processing, and acoustic models to identify, measure, and monitor the severity of depression and anxiety from short samples of natural speech. Its flagship product, Sage, is an emotionally intelligent, agentic AI care manager that conducts 24/7 patient-engagement calls for health plans, health systems, specialty care, and pharma, handling program enrollment, benefits verification, clinical assessments and surveys, and care coordination. Sage is powered by Ellipsis' patented Empathy Engine, trained on millions of live clinical patient calls, and runs on HIPAA and SOC 2 Type 2 compliant infrastructure. Ellipsis Health integrates with health plans and systems such as Cigna, and exposes a private partner API (used by partners like Augmedix) rather than a public developer platform. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, and CVS Health Ventures.

providers.name: HumanFirst
providers.description: HumanFirst is a digital health measurement company whose Atlas platform helps clinical research and life-sciences teams evaluate, select, and operationalize sensor-based digital health technologies — wearables, connected devices, and digital biomarkers — for clinical trials and real-world evidence. Atlas curates a knowledge network of digital measures, connected devices, and the published evidence behind them so sponsors and CROs can choose fit-for-purpose measures. HumanFirst is now part of ICON plc and integrated into ICON's Digital Health Technologies (DHT) capabilities. The Atlas platform is delivered as an authenticated web application at app.gohumanfirst.com; the company does not currently publish a public developer API. This profile captures the company's public identity, security, and compliance posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lena Health
providers.description: Lena Health is a Houston, Texas healthcare technology company founded in the Texas Medical Center that combines AI agents with human care navigators to deliver care coordination at scale. Its LenaConnect platform handles routine patient outreach calls, appointment scheduling and coordination, payer and provider hold times, automatic call documentation, EHR integration, and resource and referral management, so human navigators can focus on building trust with patients. Lena offers fully managed care navigation services covering Chronic Care Management (CCM), Transitional Care Management (TCM), rising-risk care management, and annual wellness visits, and works with health plans, accountable care organizations (ACOs), health systems, provider groups, care management providers, and community organizations. The company reports retrospective matched-cohort results of 29% fewer unplanned readmissions, 42% fewer ED visits, and $3,116 saved per patient within 180 days. Lena Health is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, and publishes a trust center. Lena Health is a Techstars portfolio company. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment; the platform is delivered as a managed service with EHR integration handled through engagements.

providers.name: Medigate
providers.description: Medigate was a healthcare IoT / connected-medical-device cybersecurity company (headquartered in Brooklyn, NY, backed by Partech and others) that built the first security platform dedicated to healthcare IoT — device discovery, risk assessment, and clinically-aware network segmentation for hospitals. Claroty completed its acquisition of Medigate on 2022-01-10 and folded the product into "Claroty xDome for Healthcare"; the standalone brand is retired and medigate.io now redirects to claroty.com. A residual customer-facing REST API remains live at api.medigate.io (with a password-gated interactive reference at api.medigate.io/docs) that integrations use to pull device inventory, device groups, and device risk scores.

providers.name: Agent Request Desk
providers.description: Agent Request Desk provides a free MCP server that helps AI agents report and diagnose failures when accessing external sites. It captures blocked URLs, missing data, and error reasons, offering private reports without requiring accounts. The service aggregates public issue data, supports multiple client integrations (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, n8n), and supplies pointers to official APIs or datasets when available. Operated by Patrick Hussey in the UK, it aims to improve agent reliability and transparency.

providers.name: CARET Legal
providers.description: CARET Legal provides cloud‑based legal practice management software designed to streamline case handling, automate workflows, and integrate billing, document management, and client communication. The platform serves law firms of all sizes, offering features such as case management, reporting and analytics, secure document storage, and mobile access, all hosted securely in the cloud.

providers.name: Clipboard Health
providers.description: Clipboard Health (now branded simply "Clipboard", at clipboardworks.com) is a U.S. healthcare workforce marketplace that connects workplaces — long-term care facilities, home health and hospice agencies, hospitals, dental practices, and travel assignments — with vetted, independent professionals to fill open shifts. Workplaces post shifts and Clipboard matches, credentials, schedules, and pays qualified workers, with the platform handling documentation, compliance, and instant pay for pros. The company reports serving more than 6,500 workplaces and over a million workers nationwide. Backed by Initialized Capital and IVP, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company. Clipboard Health publishes no public consumer API; its public developer surface is limited to open-source TypeScript utility libraries on npm (the @clipboard-health scope, from github.com/ClipboardHealth/core-utils) and a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Proxy
providers.description: Proxy (Y Combinator, Summer 2016) was a San Francisco digital-identity startup founded by Denis Mars and Simon Ratner that built a mobile and wearable digital wallet for payments, identity, and authentication, later expanding into biometric identity verification and vaccine-credential verification. The company was acquired by OURA in 2023; the proxy.com domain no longer resolves to an active product and there is no public developer platform, API, or documentation surface to enrich. This profile is retained as a historical/acquired-company record.

providers.name: Guardhat
providers.description: Guardhat (now operating as Aatmunn) is an industrial safety and asset intelligence platform serving more than 250 companies across oil & gas, utilities, logistics and warehousing, chemicals, mining, infrastructure, and manufacturing. Its SPANR platform is a unified intelligence layer that collects data from connected safety devices and wearables, normalizes it into a single source of truth, applies business logic, and surfaces insights through a suite of applications for digital safety inspections, lone worker safety, gas detection, human condition monitoring, control access zoning, and asset tracking. Originally known for connected hard hats and wearable safety technology, the company rebranded from Guardhat to Aatmunn. Guardhat is a venture-backed portfolio company of General Catalyst. This profile has been enriched from the company's public web presence; no public developer API or OpenAPI surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Impulse Dynamics
providers.description: Impulse Dynamics is a medical-device company that created Cardiac Contractility Modulation (CCM) therapy, delivered by the implantable Optimizer Smart and Optimizer Smart Mini pulse generators for patients with moderate-to-severe chronic heart failure who remain symptomatic despite guideline-directed medical therapy. Incorporated in 1997, with US headquarters in Marlton, New Jersey, the company won the first-ever FDA Breakthrough Device designation and received FDA approval for the Optimizer Smart in March 2019; the device has been CE marked since October 2016 and is now approved in more than 30 countries plus China. Impulse Dynamics operates no developer programme: there is no developer portal, API documentation, API reference, SDK, CLI, sandbox, pricing or sign-up, and nothing clinical or device-related is exposed as an API. It is catalogued here because its corporate website runs a live, anonymous, self-describing WordPress REST API advertising 420 routes across 30 namespaces, because that same install exposes two Model Context Protocol servers, and because the company publishes a substantive vulnerability disclosure programme with two PGP-published security contacts covering its medical devices, health software and infrastructure.

providers.name: kyanitelabs-tech
providers.description: KyaniteLabs helps builders and teams get open-source AI tools, MCP systems, media pipelines, localization QA, and repo diagnostics working in their real environment. The company provides a public API for discovery, contact, newsletter, and implementation intake workflows, exposing endpoints for health checks and an OpenAPI specification. Their platform focuses on integrating AI tools into production pipelines, offering resources such as documentation, blog posts, and open-source repositories.

providers.name: Latent
providers.description: Latent (Latent Health) is an enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform for health systems, built around a clinical agentic engine that reads the chart, reasons over payer policy and drug labels, and acts inside the electronic health record. The platform spans four modules — Identify (care-gap identification, eligibility screening, site-of-care routing), Access (prior authorization, clinical review, appeals generation, benefit routing, payer outreach), Capture (340B eligibility auditing, leakage analytics, financial dashboards), and Engage (patient outreach, queue management, outcomes analytics). Latent is chart-native and EHR agnostic, integrating with Epic, Cerner and others, and is used by more than 45 health systems including Ochsner Health, MetroHealth, Yale New Haven Health, St. Luke's Health System and Henry Ford Health, serving over two million patients annually. Founded by Sriram Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, the company has raised $80M from Spark Capital, Transformation Capital, McKesson Ventures, Conviction, General Catalyst and Y Combinator. Latent publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; its integration surface is delivered through EHR-native deployment with health-system customers, and its security posture is published on a Vanta-hosted trust center with HIPAA-compliant data handling.

providers.name: Mabel
providers.description: Mabel is a healthcare technology company (Irvine, California; backed by 500 Global) that helps Medicare accountable care organizations (ACOs) enroll and engage beneficiaries. Its platform is a market leader in voluntary alignment, used by roughly one in three ACOs, and spans four core solutions: Voluntary Alignment (campaign execution, response processing, analytics, and compliance auditing for LEAD, ACO REACH, and GUIDE programs), Health Surveys (social determinants of health screenings, NPS, and custom surveys with CMS-formatted reporting), Beneficiary Notifications (compliance notices via email, mail, or SMS with audit-ready tracking), and Letters From Your Doctor (provider-based outreach for enrollment, surveys, and appointments). Mabel is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. No public developer API or SDK surface is published at this time; this profile captures the company's identity, compliance posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Plume Health
providers.description: Plume Health (Plume) is a telehealth company delivering gender-affirming care to transgender and gender non-conforming people across the United States. Through a mobile app and licensed clinicians, Plume provides gender-affirming hormone therapy (estrogen and testosterone), mental health support, medical letters for surgery and identification changes, and everyday clinical care, all on a monthly membership subscription. Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, Plume operates as a HIPAA-covered, LegitScript-certified consumer healthcare provider. It is a consumer-facing care service and does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Rivet Health
providers.description: Rivet Health is a cloud-based revenue cycle management (RCM) platform for healthcare providers, spanning practices, specialty groups, and hospitals. Its software brings together three core modules: Revenue Diagnostics (AI-driven revenue forecasting, real-time reporting, and denial prevention), Payer Performance (contract management, payer benchmarking, and fee-schedule administration), and Patient Pricing (automated patient cost estimates and No Surprises Act Good Faith Estimates). Rivet describes itself as an agnostic platform that integrates with 30+ practice-management systems, EHRs, and clearinghouses — including Epic, athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, AdvancedMD, Veradigm, ModMed, Greenway Health, Nextech, Availity, and Change Healthcare. The company is backed by Menlo Ventures. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation; integrations are delivered through its partner network. Rivet publishes a trust center documenting SOC 2 and HIPAA posture.

providers.name: St. Jude Medical
providers.description: St. Jude Medical was a global medical device company specializing in cardiovascular devices including implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs), pacemakers, cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) devices, and electrophysiology products. The company was acquired by Abbott in January 2017 and now operates as Abbott's cardiac rhythm management division. Its flagship remote monitoring platform, Merlin.net Patient Care Network, enables clinicians to remotely monitor patients with implanted cardiac devices via the Merlin@home transmitter and the myMerlinPulse mobile application.

providers.name: Clara 2
providers.description: Clara is an AI-powered primary care and longevity practice, founded by the team behind Circle Medical and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and A.Capital. Clara pairs deep clinical AI with board-certified clinician review: it securely imports and analyzes a patient's medical records, surfaces health trends, assists with symptom assessment, medication refills, lab ordering, and longevity/biomarker goals, and routes every medical recommendation to a licensed clinician for review and approval before it reaches the patient. The company operates as a fully licensed primary care practice across all 50 U.S. states and is a HIPAA-covered entity. Clara is a consumer telehealth product (subscription plans on askclara.com) and currently publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity, trust, and compliance surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Pointone
providers.description: PointOne is an AI-powered legal practice management platform that automates time entry, billing compliance, and analytics for law firms. Its products include PointOne Time (automatic cross-device time capture with AI-generated narratives), PointOne Review (pre-bill review with AI markup and collaboration), and PointOne Intelligence (time analytics and resource-allocation insights), along with automatic enforcement of Outside Counsel Guidelines. The platform syncs with billing systems including Aderant, Clio, Filevine, QuickBooks, Actionstep, Elite 3E, Surepoint, MyCase, and LeanLaw, and serves 200+ law firms. PointOne is backed by Bessemer, Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and 8VC. No public developer API is currently published; integrations are delivered as pre-built connectors.

providers.name: Waiv
providers.description: Waiv is a Paris-based AI precision-testing company spun out of Owkin (formerly Owkin Dx) that builds clinically validated, AI-powered diagnostic tests for oncology and digital pathology. Its products — RlapsRisk BC (breast-cancer distant-relapse risk), the MSIntuit Suite (MSI/dMMR pre-screening in colorectal, gastric and endometrial cancer), BRCAura RUO (gBRCA pre-screening) and TLS Detect — read routine H&E whole-slide images to accelerate biomarker detection, outcome prediction and treatment-response assessment. The tests are delivered through Destra, an AI-native digital pathology platform that lab and clinician users reach in the browser and that laboratories can wire into an existing IMS/LIS through the Destra API. RlapsRisk BC and MSIntuit CRC hold dual CE-IVD marking under the EU IVDR. Waiv raised $33M led by OTB Ventures and Alpha Intelligence Capital, with Serena, Karista and SistaFund participating, and later closed $35M total with CRB Health Tech. The Destra API is advertised on the product page but is sales-gated — there is no public developer portal, reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Neko Health
providers.description: Neko Health is a Swedish preventive-healthcare company founded in 2018 by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne. It designs, engineers, and assembles its own full-body scanning hardware in Stockholm and operates clinics across Sweden, the UK (London, Manchester, Birmingham) and, following a $700M Series C, the United States. The roughly 60-minute Neko Health Scan is a non-invasive, radiation-free examination that captures millions of data points across the skin, heart, blood, and circulation in a single visit, feeding a consumer patient app. Neko exposes no public third-party developer API; its only public machine surface is a Duende IdentityServer OIDC provider (account.nekohealth.com) that authenticates the patient application. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched from Neko's public web and identity surface.

providers.name: Arine
providers.description: Arine is a San Francisco-based healthcare technology company that operates an AI-driven medication intelligence and comprehensive medication management platform for health plans, government payors and risk-bearing provider organizations. The platform ingests pharmacy and medical claims, clinical, cost, quality, behavioral and social-determinants-of-health data, then applies machine learning and clinical decision logic to surface medication-related gaps in care and generate targeted, just-in-time interventions, member education materials and prescriber communications. Arine packages this as four solutions — LUMINATE (high-risk member management), RESONATE (prescriber analytics), ELEVATE (Star Ratings and quality improvement) and ELEVATE MTM (medication therapy management) — delivered as a SaaS portal running in AWS. The Arine Platform holds HITRUST Risk-based 2-year (r2) certification. Arine ships no public developer program: its API gateway at api.arine.io is closed to anonymous callers and its product documentation portal at docs.arine.io sits behind customer authentication, so no machine-readable API contract is publicly available.

providers.name: Findoctave
providers.description: Findoctave (operating as Octave) is a mental health care provider offering virtual and in-person therapy across 20+ U.S. states. Services include individual, couples, and family therapy, DBT, and specialized centers of excellence for perinatal and postpartum health, LGBTQIA+ (queer resiliency), trauma, and women's emotional health. Octave is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Shield of California, BCBS plans, Health Net, and others) and publishes a therapist directory, cost calculator, and getting-started flow through its consumer website. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and added to the API Evangelist network; Octave exposes no public developer API, so this profile is a company identity record rather than an API listing.

providers.name: Juno Chat
providers.description: Juno (junocompanion.com), operated by SharedGenes, Inc., is a Y Combinator-backed (P26) consumer digital-health startup building an AI personal health assistant for the 1B+ people living with chronic illness. The Juno mobile app (iOS and Android) builds a longitudinal health profile through conversation, biometrics, and medical history to deliver personalized symptom guidance, automated symptom tracking by text or voice, trigger-pattern identification, and appointment-ready reports for clinicians. It supports conditions including fibromyalgia, long COVID, POTS, ME/CFS, EDS, endometriosis, lupus, and MS, and is informed by research from Oxford and UCL plus 1,000+ patient interviews. Founded in 2025 by Marshall Gould (CEO) and Isaac Tolley (CTO); HIPAA-aligned infrastructure with no health data sold. Juno also publishes Juno Open Health Tools, an MIT-licensed remote MCP server at https://juno-health-tools.vercel.app/api/mcp with five read-only, consent-gated tools that turn a user's non-identifying health notes into non-diagnostic appointment-preparation material; it is listed in the official MCP Registry and archived on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21730086). Juno publishes no REST API or SDK.

providers.name: Lighten
providers.description: Lighten Platforms, Inc. is a San Mateo, California healthcare AI company building an AI-native platform for clinical evidence curation from electronic health record (EHR) data. Its 360° EHR Curation Platform reasons over unstructured clinical notes together with structured records to reconstruct complete patient journeys, applying clinically validated quality assurance at the variable, patient, and cohort level rather than relying on model accuracy metrics alone. On top of that curation layer Lighten delivers Apps & Insights for patient finding and HCP targeting, longitudinal patient journeys, and market intelligence, plus a "Beyond Claims" offering that integrates curated EHR signal with claims data for broader coverage. The company serves life sciences, health systems, data and analytics consultancies, and investors, and was founded by Xinkun Nie, PhD. Lighten publishes no public developer API program, SDKs, or developer documentation as of this profile.

providers.name: MTN OPS
providers.description: MTN OPS is an American-owned outdoor performance nutrition and lifestyle brand founded in 2014 and headquartered in Fruit Heights, Utah. The company develops, manufactures, and sells energy and nutrition supplements (pre-workout, protein, hydration, creatine, and energy bars) alongside apparel and gear for hunters, tactical professionals, military, and outdoor athletes, running a "Conquer Hunger" program that donates one meal for every order placed. MTN OPS is a direct-to-consumer, internet-first retailer operating on the Shopify platform and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. It publishes no bespoke developer API; the only machine-readable surfaces on its domain are the Shopify New Customer Accounts OIDC discovery documents and a Shopify-generated agent-commerce llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Norwest portfolio lead and enriched from the provider's live public surface.

providers.name: 9am Health
providers.description: 9amHealth (join9am.com) is a US virtual cardiometabolic clinic delivering specialized care for type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight loss, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol entirely from home. Founded in 2021 in San Diego by mySugr co-founders Frank Westermann and Anton Kittelberger, the company pairs at-home lab test kits, asynchronous and synchronous telehealth visits with obesity specialists, pharmacists, dietitians, and behavioral health experts, mail-order pharmacy for prescriptions including GLP-1 receptor agonists, and optional connected devices such as continuous glucose monitors into individualized care plans. It sells direct to individuals and through employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers. 9amHealth is a consumer and enterprise telehealth brand and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public web identity for the API Evangelist network. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Forus
providers.description: Forus (formerly Tandem) is an AI-powered healthcare technology company operating a network that connects physicians, pharmacies, payers, and biopharmaceutical companies to accelerate patient access to prescribed medicines. Its platform automates the administrative work between a clinical decision and treatment initiation: insurance prior authorization, AI-generated denial appeals, financial-assistance enrollment, benefit verification, and pharmacy fulfillment routing. Forus is embedded in physician workflows across most U.S. zip codes and is SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant. It offers no public developer API, OpenAPI spec, or SDKs; this profile captures the company's public web, trust, and security surface.

providers.name: HealthJoy
providers.description: HealthJoy is a Chicago-based employee-benefits engagement, healthcare navigation, and cost-containment platform founded in 2014, which markets itself as a "Benefits Operating System" (BOS) for employers and benefit consultants. It unifies fragmented health benefits into a single member-facing app combining Joy AI — a 24/7 AI assistant trained on each client's benefits plan — with a licensed human healthcare concierge team, provider search with cost scores and quality ratings, prescription savings, medical bill review, and an intelligent steerage engine that routes members to high-value, fair-priced care. Employers and consultants get a client dashboard reporting engagement, utilization, savings, and ROI. HealthJoy reports 1,800+ client companies and 1.25M+ members. It publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract; integrations with benefits-administration and TPA vendors (e.g. Employee Navigator) are delivered as managed eligibility/census data feeds set up by its implementation team rather than as a self-serve API.

providers.name: Invitae
providers.description: Invitae — operated as Labcorp Invitae / Labcorp Genetics since Labcorp acquired select Invitae assets out of the company's 2024 Chapter 11 — is a United States medical genetics and healthcare-technology company providing clinical-grade hereditary and somatic genetic testing across oncology, women's health, cardiology, neurology, pediatrics, and rare disease. Its laboratory is CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited, and it publishes a HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices and state laboratory licensure. Clinicians order tests and receive results through a web portal with licensed genetic counseling and the Gia digital assistant. Invitae publishes no API: contract discovery across every Invitae host found no developer portal, no OpenAPI, no GraphQL endpoint, no MCP server, no A2A agent card, no FHIR CapabilityStatement, no SMART-on-FHIR configuration, no webhooks, no client SDK and no /.well-known document. api.invitae.com resolves but returns a blanket nginx 403 for every path, and the developer, docs and fhir subdomains do not resolve at all. The company's public GitHub organization is genuine but consists of forks of upstream bioinformatics projects, not first-party specifications or libraries.

providers.name: MORE Health
providers.description: MORE Health, Inc. is a global digital health company headquartered in San Mateo, California, with offices in Boston, Houston, New York, Beijing, Shanghai, Chengdu and Guangzhou. It provides expert medical second opinions and cross-border telemedicine through its proprietary, cloud-based Physician Collaboration Platform, which lets a patient's treating physician and an expert specialist jointly review medical history, hospital records, lab results, DICOM imaging, pathology imaging and genetic testing, and co-develop a diagnosis and treatment plan over HIPAA-compliant video conferencing with translation in 129 languages. Product lines include Expert Medical Opinion, MORE Health for Kids, employee benefits for self-insured groups, a Medical Travel Concierge, mental health, Prodigy Fertility and hospital solutions for health systems seeking international patient reach. The company states it serves 6.2 million members across six continents and that its platform is ISO 27001 certified and GDPR- and HIPAA-compliant. MORE Health publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification of any kind; the platform is sold to patients, employers and hospitals as an end-user product.

providers.name: Butterfly Network
providers.description: Butterfly Network develops handheld, portable ultrasound devices and a cloud‑based imaging platform that enable clinicians to capture, store, and share diagnostic images at the point of care. The company offers a suite of products including the iQ series of probes, AI‑assisted image analysis, and a subscription service for data management and tele‑medicine integration, serving hospitals, clinics, and veterinary practices worldwide.

providers.name: Fortuna Health
providers.description: Fortuna Health is a consumer-first Medicaid navigation platform that helps patients and members move through the Medicaid enrollment, recertification, appeals, and coverage-management processes end to end. Founded in 2023 and based in New York City, Fortuna consolidates the fragmented rules of the 50+ state and territory Medicaid programs — each with its own eligibility rules, documentation standards, and renewal timelines — into a single digital interface. The platform lets consumers connect accounts that auto-populate their filings, provides a virtual mailbox for state and health-plan communications, and sends text notifications for urgent, time-sensitive actions. Fortuna partners with health systems and managed care plans as middleware for the roughly $800B Medicaid ecosystem, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Little Spoon
providers.description: Little Spoon is a New York-based direct-to-consumer children's food and nutrition brand, founded in 2017, that delivers fresh, organic, stage-based meals, snacks and infant formula for babies, toddlers and kids on a subscription basis across the United States. Its product architecture maps to feeding stages — Formula, Babyblends purees, Biteables finger foods, Baby Puffs, Baby Cereal, Smoothies and YoGos, Lunchers, Plates and a snack line — with a frozen line sold exclusively through Target. The brand competes on ingredient transparency: a published No-No List of 100+ banned ingredients, EU-level food safety standards, 500+ toxin and contaminant tests, and 2000+ safety tests per batch of Formula. Little Spoon operates no public developer program and publishes no API contract; its storefront is a Next.js front end backed by an undocumented first-party JSON API at api.littlespoon.com. It does publish two machine-readable public artifacts — an llms.txt at the site root and an open-source React design system distributed as fifteen @littlespoon/* npm packages from the little-spoon-dev GitHub org.

providers.name: Tabs3
providers.description: Tabs3 provides cloud‑based practice management software for law firms, offering integrated billing, accounting, case management, and reporting tools. Their platform helps legal professionals improve profitability, streamline workflows, and maintain compliance with trust accounting standards, serving thousands of firms worldwide.

providers.name: Vetcove
providers.description: Vetcove is a free purchasing and procurement platform for veterinary clinics and animal-health organizations that lets a practice shop every distributor and manufacturer at once. It consolidates accounts from suppliers such as Henry Schein, Patterson Vet, MWI, and Midwest Veterinary into one interface where staff compare live pricing and availability, place and track orders, and manage inventory across vendors without changing existing supplier relationships. The service is delivered as a web application and mobile app and is free to veterinary clinics and nonprofits. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company identity and a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Woebot Health
providers.description: Woebot Health is a clinical mental health company founded in 2017 by Dr. Alison Darcy that delivers an AI-powered, CBT-based conversational agent ("Woebot") for evidence-based mental health support. The company operates an enterprise (B2B) model, partnering with health systems, payers, employers, and providers to embed Woebot into existing care pathways and digital front doors. The Woebot Health Platform offers a partner API library for transmitting aggregated, validated patient-reported outcomes (PHQ-8/PHQ-9, engagement, satisfaction, topic modeling) into EMRs and value-based care workflows. The partner API is gated to enterprise customers — there is no public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: Workit Health
providers.description: Workit Health is a 100% virtual addiction-treatment provider delivering telehealth care for opioid use disorder, alcohol use disorder, and kratom/7-OH dependence via mobile app and video visits with licensed clinicians. Care includes FDA-approved medications such as Suboxone (buprenorphine/naloxone) and naltrexone, recovery groups, and asynchronous care-team messaging, serving members across fourteen US states. Backed by Insight Partners and Lux Capital. Workit Health publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: CUTISS
providers.description: CUTISS AG is a Swiss late-stage clinical TechBio company headquartered at the Bio-Technopark in Schlieren, Zurich, founded in 2017 as a spin-off of the Tissue Biology Research Unit (TBRU) at the University of Zurich and the University Children's Hospital Zurich, and accelerated through Wyss Zurich. Its lead product, denovoSkin, is a first-in-class bioengineered, personalized dermo-epidermal skin graft grown from a small biopsy of a patient's own skin to treat large and deep skin defects in children and adults; it holds Orphan Drug Designation for burns from Swissmedic, the EMA and the FDA and is in late-stage clinical development. With CSEM the company built denovoCast, described as the world's first machine for automated production of personalized human skin tissue, funded in part by Innosuisse and EU Horizon 2020. CUTISS has raised roughly CHF 50 million and employs around 50 people. It is a therapeutics manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no product API, no developer portal, no SDKs and no pricing. The only machine-readable API on its public host is the WordPress REST API behind cutiss.swiss, which serves the newsroom, blog, corporate pages, team directory, teams taxonomy and media library as JSON, read-only without credentials.

providers.name: Joy
providers.description: Joy offers a subscription-based parenting club that provides expert‑backed toolkits, 24/7 human support, personalized insights, and 1:1 video consultations for parents in the United States. Members can track daily baby activities, access resources on feeding, sleep, behavior, and receive exclusive discounts on family products.

providers.name: Superpower
providers.description: Superpower is a consumer preventive-health and longevity membership that provides an annual comprehensive blood draw across 100+ biomarkers, AI-driven result interpretation, biological age scoring, personalized action plans, and a care team, delivered through web and mobile apps. As of the catalog date Superpower does not publish a public or partner developer API; this catalog documents the product surface honestly rather than fabricating endpoints.

providers.name: 98point6 Technologies
providers.description: 98point6 Technologies is a Seattle-based digital health software company, founded in 2015, that builds and licenses a cloud-based virtual care platform to health systems, payers and virtual care providers. After selling its own care-delivery division in 2023 it operates purely as a licensed software provider. The platform combines an AI-driven Automated Assistant for patient intake and visit documentation, a web-based Clinician Console with automated clinical decision support, and a white-labeled patient application, covering both asynchronous and real-time (messaging, audio, video) care. It advertises HL7 and FHIR based EMR integration with Epic and Cerner, SSO for patient login, and an SDK for building a fully branded patient experience, but that integration surface is delivered under a licensing agreement, so no developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification is published publicly.

providers.name: Acadia Healthcare
providers.description: Acadia Healthcare Company, Inc. (NASDAQ: ACHC) is a Franklin, Tennessee-based Fortune 1000 behavioral healthcare provider operating a national network of acute inpatient psychiatric hospitals, specialty substance use disorder treatment facilities, residential treatment centers, and outpatient comprehensive treatment clinics across the United States. It is a clinical services operator rather than a software company: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable contract of any kind. A MuleSoft CloudHub gateway is deployed at api.acadiahealthcare.com, but every anonymous path on it returns an empty-body HTTP 404, and the developer host previously recorded here (developer.acadiahealthcare.com) does not resolve. Not to be confused with Acadia Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: ACAD), an unrelated company.

providers.name: Basata
providers.description: Basata is a Phoenix-based healthcare AI company building the operational layer for American medical practices. Its AI agents automate back-office administrative work — processing patient referrals, answering phone calls 24/7, and managing faxes and patient communications — while integrating with existing EHR systems so clinical staff can focus on patient care instead of paperwork. Founded in 2024 by Kaled Alhanafi (CEO, formerly Lyft and Cruise), Chetan Patel (co-founder and president, formerly Medtronic), and Vivin Paliath (co-founder and CTO), Basata raised a $21M Series A led by Basis Set Ventures with Cowboy Ventures and PHX Ventures participating (~$24.5M total). The platform is marketed as fully HIPAA-compliant and the company publishes a SOC 2 attestation. Basata does not currently expose a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: Brightseed
providers.description: Brightseed is a bioactives and AI company founded in 2017 (San Francisco, CA, with operations in Durham, NC) that uses its Forager AI platform to map the compounds in plants to human biological pathways and health benefits. Forager draws on a proprietary dataset the company describes as the world's largest — 21 million bioactive compounds and hundreds of biological receptors spanning 23 health areas — combining high-resolution omics, high-throughput robotics and machine learning to predict which natural compounds confer a benefit and where to source them at commercial scale. Hummingbird, launched in 2026, layers an agentic AI system on top of Forager to carry partners from discovery through development. Brightseed sells discovery services (Bioactive Profiler, Bioactive Ingredient Finder) and market-ready ingredients (Bio Gut Fiber, Bio Meta Control, Bio Gut Core) to food, supplement and health-science companies. Brightseed publishes no product or developer API for Forager or Hummingbird — those are sold as enterprise engagements through a contact form. The single machine-readable surface the company operates is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) behind its corporate site at www.brightseedbio.com, which exposes anonymous read access to posts, pages, categories, tags, users, media, comments, search, taxonomies, types and statuses, plus authenticated write operations via WordPress application passwords. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from that live surface.

providers.name: Camber
providers.description: Camber is a healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) and medical billing software platform purpose-built for specialty care providers, including ABA (applied behavior analysis) therapy, physical therapy, and ENT and allergy clinics. The platform automates the full claims lifecycle — creation and submission, pre-submission scrubbing and eligibility verification, payment posting and reconciliation, and denial management and prevention — using a rules engine and AI trained on billions of dollars in real claims data, combined with human review where judgment matters. Founded in 2021 (Y Combinator W21, rebranded from Juniper Behavioral Health to Camber), the New York-based company is backed by Craft Ventures, a16z, and Y Combinator, and processes over a million claims annually for hundreds of specialty care providers across all 50 states.

providers.name: Lively
providers.description: Lively is a fintech-healthtech company that provides modern, cloud-based Health Savings Accounts (HSA) alongside Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), Health Reimbursement Arrangements (HRA), COBRA, and commuter benefits for individuals, families, employers, benefits administrators, and third-party administrators. Lively pairs interest-bearing and investment-enabled HSAs (via a Schwab Health Savings Brokerage Account and a guided HSA portfolio) with an employer dashboard for contributions and administration, positioning itself around transparent, zero-hidden-fee pricing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures and GGV Capital, Lively integrates with benefit administration platforms and third-party administrators but does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is handled through its sales and partnerships channels. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Lively's public web surface.

providers.name: RapidClaims
providers.description: RapidClaims is a healthcare revenue-cycle-management (RCM) company building autonomous AI agents for medical coding and claims. Its platform automates medical coding (RapidCode), value-based-care coding and risk adjustment (RapidVBC), denial management and revenue recovery (RapidRecovery), and a unified revenue cycle platform (RapidRCM) for FQHCs, community health centers, ACOs, physician groups, ambulatory surgery centers, hospitals, and management services organizations. The company emphasizes a healthcare-grade security and compliance posture (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2 Type II, 256-bit encryption). RapidClaims is backed by Accel and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Tava Health
providers.description: Tava Health, Inc. is a Utah-founded (2019) digital behavioral-health company that sells mental health care as an employer and health-plan benefit. Employers, health plans and provider groups contract with Tava; covered members are matched to a licensed therapist — typically within about twelve hours — and receive care over secure video or in person through a nationwide clinical network. Care is delivered by Tava Professionals, a set of state-level professional entities that act as the HIPAA covered entity, while Tava Health, Inc. operates the technology platform as their business associate. The platform runs as two portals: a client portal at care.tavahealth.com for members and a provider/administrative portal at app.tavahealth.com for therapists and plan administrators. Tava also runs DirectCare, a partner-facing product with its own developer hub at docs.tavahealth.com; that hub is a ReadMe.io site and is password-protected, so no public API reference, OpenAPI definition or other machine-readable contract is available at this time.

providers.name: Boundless Bio
providers.description: Boundless Bio (Nasdaq: BOLD) is a San Diego, California based clinical-stage, next-generation precision oncology company founded in 2018 to target extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) — circular, centromere-free DNA that carries high copy-number oncogene amplifications and is observed in roughly 17% of cancer patients, driving tumor heterogeneity and resistance to targeted therapy. Its proprietary Spyglass discovery platform, built on a suite of ecDNA+/- tumor models plus molecular analytics and imaging, identifies targets essential to ecDNA function, which the company drugs with small-molecule ecDNA-directed therapies (ecDTx). The clinical pipeline is led by BBI-940, a kinesin inhibitor targeting ecDNA segregation, in the Phase 1 KOMODO-1 trial in ER+/HER2- and TNBC-LAR breast cancer opened in February 2026, with earlier CHK1 (replication stress) and RNR (DNA assembly and repair) programs behind it; ECHO, its ecDNA diagnostic algorithm, reads ecDNA off routine clinical next-generation sequencing and is described by the company as the first ecDNA diagnostic used in clinical trials. Boundless Bio raised a $100M Series C co-led by Leaps by Bayer and RA Capital and listed on Nasdaq in 2024. It publishes no developer program, no product API, no SDKs and no API documentation of any kind; the only machine-readable surface on boundlessbio.com is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2), anonymously readable, which serves the corporate pages, the Leadership directory and the media library as JSON.

providers.name: BrightSpring Health Services
providers.description: BrightSpring Health Services is a leading Fortune 500 provider of comprehensive home and community-based health services for complex populations. The company operates across three primary service lines: Provider Services (home health, rehabilitation, neurorehabilitation, personal care), Pharmacy Services (specialty infusion, home and community-based pharmacy dispensing over 40 million prescriptions annually), and Managed Care (home-based primary care with demonstrated 44% reduction in hospitalizations). BrightSpring operates multiple clinical brands including Adoration Home Health, Amerita specialty infusion, and All Ways Caring.

providers.name: Eleos Health
providers.description: Eleos Health is the most widely adopted AI platform in behavioral and community-based healthcare. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, Eleos delivers purpose-built AI workflow agents that span clinical documentation, compliance, and revenue cycle management. The platform embeds directly inside providers' existing web-based electronic health records (EHRs) via a lightweight browser extension for both in-person and telehealth sessions, turning ambient session capture or quick text summaries into structured, payer-ready progress notes and cutting documentation time by roughly 70%. Eleos Compliance reviews every note against common risk areas (note cloning, empty notes, interventions, progress mentions, action plans, and the golden thread), and its revenue cycle tooling automates eligibility checks and claim protection. Deployed across 120+ care organizations in 30+ states, Eleos integrates without custom API builds; it is backed by Menlo Ventures and Greenfield Partners.

providers.name: QUIBIM
providers.description: QUIBIM is a healthcare AI company that unlocks medical imaging data to improve patient outcomes through quantitative imaging biomarkers and radiomics. Its cloud-based, tissue-agnostic platform ingests, harmonizes, and analyzes imaging data (MRI, CT, PET) to extract automated radiomics and deep-learning imaging biomarkers that support clinical decision-making and biopharma drug development. Regulated clinical products include QP-Prostate, QP-Brain, QP-Liver, QP-Breast, QP-Lung, and the QP-Insights multi-omics platform, several of which are CE and UKCA marked and integrate with hospital PACS systems. QUIBIM is ISO 27001:2022 certified and HIPAA and GDPR compliant. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; QUIBIM publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Spectrum Medical
providers.description: Spectrum Medical is a privately held medical technology company, co-founded by Steve Turner and Mark Drain, with corporate headquarters in Cheltenham, England, a U.S. headquarters in Fort Mill, South Carolina, and a European headquarters in Mirandola, Italy. It entered the global medical device market in 2005 with its non-invasive System M diagnostic technology and today builds two connected product families: Quantum Perfusion Technologies (workstations, centrifugal and roller pumps, oxygenators, heater-coolers, sensor modules and single-use sterile technologies for cardiopulmonary bypass, ECMO and other extracorporeal therapies) and Quantum Informatics (the VIPER clinical interfacing EMR, the VISION server and Perfusion Information Management System). Its software surface is a customer-deployed, on-premise stack: the VISION server passes case data to the hospital EHR over HL7 v2 interfaces through a bundled Mirth Connect interface engine, and third-party device connectivity is delivered through optional device-driver software rather than a public web API. Spectrum Medical is ISO/IEC 27001:2013 certified and its VIPER Clinical Information Solution 3.0 earned ONC-HIT 2014 Edition Modular Certification via the Drummond Group. Systems are in use in over 60 countries.

providers.name: C. R. Bard
providers.description: C. R. Bard, Inc. was an American multinational developer, manufacturer, and marketer of medical technologies in the fields of vascular, urology, oncology, and surgical specialties. Bard was founded in 1907 by Charles Russell Bard and was acquired by Becton, Dickinson and Company (BD) in December 2017 for approximately $24 billion. Bard's product lines now operate as part of BD's Interventional segment under the BD Bard brand. No public API or developer portal is published; integrations with hospital and provider systems are arranged through BD enterprise channels.

providers.name: Dutch
providers.description: Dutch (dutch.com) is a United States pet telemedicine service that gives dog and cat owners 24/7 access to licensed online veterinarians through a low-cost membership (from about $11/month), pairing virtual vet visits with free prescription delivery to most states. Founded to bring the direct-to-consumer telehealth model to pet care, Dutch is backed by Forerunner Ventures. The public presence is a consumer telehealth storefront hosted on Shopify; at the time of profiling no first-party public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface was found. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's real, published web surface (identity, policies, account, support) and the live platform-level discovery documents exposed on the domain.

providers.name: House Rx
providers.description: House Rx is a healthcare technology company that equips independent specialty and community clinics to run in-house, medically integrated dispensing pharmacies. Founded in 2021, its cloud platform — built by specialty pharmacists and physicians — supports the full specialty-medication workflow: prior authorization, financial counseling and copay assistance, fulfillment tools, scalable patient outreach and messaging, real-time operational analytics, and EHR integration so physicians and pharmacists collaborate on patient care. House Rx is SOC 2 compliant and backed by First Round, Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Maverick Ventures, 1984 Ventures, and Character Ventures. House Rx does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Judi Health
providers.description: Judi Health (formerly Capital Rx) is a healthcare technology company delivering unified pharmacy and medical benefit administration. Its platform, Judi, is a modern claims and benefits processing system (a Core Administrative Processing System / CAPS) that self-funded employers, unions, health plans, third-party administrators (TPAs), brokers, and health systems use to run transparent, pass-through pharmacy benefit management (Judi Rx), integrated health benefit administration (Judi Care), care navigation, level-funded pharmacy benefits, a Medicare prescription payment plan, and white-label discount cards. Judi Cloud licenses the underlying platform to other administrators. In 2026 the company rebranded from Capital Rx to Judi Health following a $400M funding round to accelerate its AI-powered health benefits platform, and its PBM business surpassed five million contracted lives. Judi Health does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference; this profile captures the company identity, web properties, and security/trust posture.

providers.name: Parachute Health
providers.description: Parachute Health is the leading digital platform for durable medical equipment (DME), home medical equipment, and medical supply ePrescribing. Clinicians eSign and submit DME orders in seconds, and the platform coordinates in real time across a network of 3,000+ supplier locations, 270,000+ eSigning clinicians, and 70,000+ facilities in all 50 states. Parachute integrates with EHR/EMR systems (athenahealth, PointClickCare, Epic, and others) using HL7 2.x and FHIR interfaces, and offers prior-authorization automation, health-plan workflows, and value-based-care coordination. Integration is delivered as private, partner-provisioned EMR/HL7/FHIR interfaces rather than a public self-service developer API.

providers.name: Sword
providers.description: Sword Health is a digital health company delivering AI-powered virtual care for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain, pelvic health, and injury prevention. Founded in 2015 in Portugal by Virgilio Bento, Sword pairs licensed physical therapists with motion-sensor and computer-vision technology so members can complete clinically supervised physical therapy from home. Its platform spans an enrollment platform, a treatment platform, a mobile application backed by a mobile API, a file-exchange platform for enterprise clients, and an AI care system. Sword serves 1,000+ enterprise and health-plan clients across three continents, is backed by investors including General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund, and Transformation Capital, and maintains SOC 2 Type 2, HITRUST, ISO 13485, HIPAA, GDPR, and Cyber Essentials compliance. Sword does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its identity, status, security, and compliance surface.

providers.name: Nolla Health
providers.description: Nolla Health is a Norway-born, AI-powered telehealth and dermatology company that entered the U.S. market with a $4.5M seed round led by General Catalyst and set up its headquarters in New York City. After treating more than 50,000 patients in Europe and becoming one of Norway's top-five medical apps, Nolla launched an AI-guided skin and acne care platform across 40+ U.S. states. The service pairs proprietary AI symptom assessment with clinician-in-the-loop oversight: patients complete a guided chat, a licensed U.S. medical provider reviews and approves every diagnosis and prescription, and topical medications are shipped directly to the patient. Nolla operates as a consumer-facing product (per-consultation and a monthly subscription) rather than an API provider, and publicly states HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

providers.name: RefleXion Medical
