providers.description: RefleXion Medical is a privately held therapeutic oncology company headquartered in Hayward, California, founded in 2009 by Sam Mazin and Akshay Nanduri around the biology-guided radiotherapy (BgRT) concept conceived at Stanford University in 2007. The company designs, manufactures and commercializes the RefleXion X1 radiotherapy platform and SCINTIX biology-guided radiotherapy, which uses onboard PET detectors to sense emissions from an injected radiopharmaceutical and autonomously direct external-beam radiotherapy delivery with sub-second latency. The RefleXion X1 received FDA clearance for SRS, SBRT and IMRT in 2020, and SCINTIX therapy was FDA cleared in February 2023 for treating tumors in the lung or bone arising from primary and metastatic cancer. RefleXion has raised more than $500 million from investors including TPG's The Rise Fund, KCK Group, PSP Investments, Sofinnova, Pfizer Ventures and Johnson & Johnson Innovation. RefleXion is a medical device manufacturer rather than a software vendor and publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Rite Aid
providers.description: Rite Aid is one of the nation's leading drugstore chains, providing prescription drugs, health and beauty aids, and convenience items. Rite Aid supports vendor integrations through EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) and B2B services, and offers digital health tools including an AI health assistant, pharmacy services, vaccination record management, and preventive health screening programs.

providers.name: Simpatico Project
providers.description: Simpatico Project (유쾌한프로젝트, Yukwaehan Project Co., Ltd.) is a Korean B2B mental-wellness startup, backed by 500 Global, whose product Clify (클라이피, "Climb & Clarify") is an AI-based integrated mental-care and Employee Assistance Program (EAP) solution for individuals and companies. Clify uses a patented multimodal algorithm to fuse Face & Voice biosignals — blood-flow changes, micro-expressions and voice characteristics — into a roughly one-minute mental-state diagnosis (stress, anxiety, depression, burnout) that it claims exceeds 90% accuracy, and rolls the results up into an organization insight dashboard for HR (company-wide mental trends, high/low-risk teams, usage). Personal mental data is processed on-device and de-identified so it is never shared with the employer, and the company states it holds ISO 27001. Product surfaces include FAV (the Face & Voice AI diagnosis engine), an EAP counseling center, and the Clify organization-insight analytics. The public presence (clify.co.kr, an imweb-built marketing and account site) exposes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Stack Health
providers.description: Stack Healthcare (stackhealthcare.com) is a health-insurance fintech offering affordable, flexible coverage for small businesses and their teams. Operating as a technology company rather than a bank, Stack acts as a HIPAA Business Associate to employer-sponsored health plans, processing Protected Health Information for enrollment and benefits administration, and partners with Stripe for payments and Celtic Bank for issuing commercial cards. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Stack publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface — the product is a waitlist-gated web application — so this profile captures the identity, security, and compliance posture that is publicly verifiable.

providers.name: Valera Health
providers.description: Valera Health is a Brooklyn, New York based virtual behavioral health provider delivering therapy, psychiatry, group therapy, comprehensive Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), suicide care and youth support programs to adults and children through an in-house clinical team, a care-coordinator model and a patient mobile app. It is a care-delivery organization rather than a software vendor: revenue comes from commercial insurance, Medicaid and Medicare reimbursement, and the clinical record and patient portal run on third-party health IT (the patient portal is operated by NextGen Healthcare at pxpportal.nextgen.com). As of this profile Valera Health publishes no developer program, no public API reference, and no machine-readable contract of any kind; its only externally addressable API host, api.valerahealth.com, is the private backend for its own patient application.

providers.name: ADOR Diagnostics
providers.description: ADOR Diagnostics is an in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) company developing syndromic multiplex molecular diagnostics for infectious disease, headquartered in Guidonia Montecelio, Italy with operations in Israel and Cyprus. Its NATlab platform pairs a bench-top modular analyser with a disposable all-included microfluidic cartridge to run fully automated sample-to-answer testing of crude clinical specimens in roughly 30-60 minutes, detecting up to 100 multiplexed targets per sample. The assay chemistry is a patented isothermal rolling circle amplification (RCA) protocol read by a proprietary carbon array sensor embedded in the cartridge, rather than PCR, and the system is aimed at small and mid-sized laboratories, doctor offices, point-of-care and near-bed testing, rural labs and mobile care units. The company markets an optional connectivity feature linking NATlab units across sites for geographic mapping of results and outbreak detection, but publishes no technical documentation for it. ADOR is a diagnostics instrument and assay manufacturer, not a software vendor: it operates no developer program, publishes no public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and the only machine-readable surfaces on its own host are an llms.txt and the Wix-platform site MCP endpoint that llms.txt advertises.

providers.name: Bevel
providers.description: Bevel is a consumer digital-health application, built by Finerpoint, Inc., that acts as an AI-powered "connected health coach." It consolidates and interprets health data from wearables (Apple Watch, Oura, Garmin, Amazfit) and lab providers (Labcorp, Quest, LifeLabs) into a single view, scoring daily strain, sleep, recovery, stress/energy, nutrition, cycle, biological age and strength training. Its "Bevel Intelligence" layer delivers conversational, research-backed guidance, personalized workout plans and daily check-ins. Bevel is a mobile-first consumer product with no publicly documented developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, roadmap and legal surface. Backed by General Catalyst.

providers.name: Carecloud
providers.description: CareCloud (NASDAQ: CCLD, formerly MTBC) is a cloud-based healthcare technology company serving 45,000+ providers with an integrated platform spanning electronic health records (EHR), practice management, revenue cycle management (RCM), patient experience tools, and AI-driven clinical documentation (cirrusAI). Its Connector product delivers healthcare interoperability with FHIR and C-CDA data exchange across labs, EHRs, immunization registries, and diagnostics. CareCloud is Drummond-certified ONC Health IT and Surescripts-certified, publishes HIPAA compliance content, and operates a developer portal (AWS API Gateway) at developer.carecloud.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Chefaa
providers.description: Chefaa is Egypt's leading digital pharmacy and pharmacy-benefits platform, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Cairo. Its GPS-enabled, AI-powered consumer app connects more than 1.5 million monthly users with a nationwide network of over 1,500 partner pharmacies, letting patients upload, order, schedule, and refill both insured and non-insured prescriptions with home delivery, medication reminders, and pharmacist chat support. On the B2B side Chefaa operates a full-stack supply layer for pharmacies and corporates — including Chefaa Supply (direct procurement with deferred payment and consolidated delivery) and the Makhazen pharmacy-supply app — plus the Chefaa Prime subscription for SMEs and consumers. Chefaa is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Chefaa publishes consumer and B2B web/mobile products but does not expose a public developer API program, so the enrichment below is limited to its public web, security, and domain surface.

providers.name: NeuroFlow
providers.description: NeuroFlow is a Philadelphia-based behavioral health technology company that gives payers, health systems, provider groups and federal agencies the infrastructure to identify and manage behavioral health risk at scale. Its IntegrateBH platform pairs patient-facing mobile and web applications with measurement-based care and screening workflows, clinical dashboards, care-coordination tooling and population-level behavioral health analytics. The platform reaches customers through EHR and partner integrations — including Epic (App Orchard / Epic Showroom) and the Xealth digital-health ecosystem — over a session-authenticated REST API served from neuroflowlive.com/api/. NeuroFlow publishes no public developer portal: a Swagger document exists at /api/swagger.json on every environment, but it returns HTTP 401 "Please log in to continue" to anonymous callers, so the contract is customer-only.

providers.name: Blooming Health
providers.description: Blooming Health is an AI-powered, omnichannel care-management and community-engagement platform for healthcare and social-services organizations. It lets teams design multilingual care workflows across voice, SMS, and email in minutes — automating screening and needs assessments, service recommendations, outreach, appointment reminders, wellness check-ins, emergency broadcasts, closed-loop referral tracking, and Medicaid/SNAP recertification. The platform integrates with existing EHR/CRM systems and databases via FHIR, HL7, API, and SFTP, and is HIPAA compliant with encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access controls, audit trails, BAAs, and SOC 2 documentation available on request. Blooming Health is a healthcare portfolio company of Insight Partners. It exposes an enterprise integration surface but publishes no public developer portal or API reference.

providers.name: Equip Health
providers.description: Equip Health is a virtual, evidence-based eating disorder treatment provider founded in 2019 by Kristina Saffran and Erin Parks. Equip delivers 100% remote, insurance-covered care for all eating disorder diagnoses — anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder (BED), ARFID, atypical anorexia, and OSFED — using Family-Based Treatment (FBT) and other evidence-based approaches. Every patient is matched with a five-person care team: a therapist, medical provider, dietitian, family mentor, and peer mentor. Equip serves patients across the United States with no waitlist, publishes an extensive library of clinical and recovery articles, partners with providers and health plans, and operates a patient portal at my.equip.health. This profile catalogs Equip's public web, legal, security, and content surfaces; Equip publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation program at this time.

providers.name: FirstVet
providers.description: FirstVet is a digital veterinary care company offering 24/7 online video consultations with licensed veterinarians for dogs, cats, and other pets. Founded in Sweden, FirstVet operates a consumer telehealth platform across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States, providing virtual vet appointments, healthy pet checkups, follow-up care, and triage guidance on whether a case needs an in-clinic referral. The company partners with pet insurers and employers to offer covered or subsidized access to its subscription-based virtual care. FirstVet is a portfolio company of Creandum. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; FirstVet publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Hello Patient
providers.description: Hello Patient builds AI agents (branded "Mia") for patient conversations across voice, text, and web chat, helping healthcare practices automate their front office, back office, and patient-growth workflows. Mia handles 24/7 appointment scheduling, insurance verification, and patient intake on the front office; revenue-cycle (RCM) follow-up and no-show recovery on the back office; and lead conversion, patient recall, and targeted outreach for growth. The platform serves dentistry, dermatology, ENT, mental health, optometry, primary care, urgent care, veterinary, and consumer-health practices, and integrates with EHR and practice systems including ModMed, AdvancedMD, NextGen, eClinicalWorks, Athena Health, Veradigm, Zenoti, and others. Hello Patient is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 Type 2 certified. It is backed by 8VC and Scale Venture Partners. No public developer API is documented at this time; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Limbic
providers.description: Limbic is a clinical AI company for mental healthcare, founded in 2020 and headquartered in New York with a London engineering base. Its two products — Limbic Access, a Class IIa (UKCA) medical device for conversational patient intake, assessment and clinical decision support, and Limbic Care, an AI companion delivering guided CBT and on-demand support between therapy sessions — are embedded by health plans, health systems, behavioral health providers and NHS Talking Therapies services. Both are built on the proprietary "Limbic Layer", a clinical reasoning layer that sits between the user and a large language model to enforce validated clinical guidance. Limbic Access embeds into a provider website with a small script snippet rather than a public developer API; the company publishes no developer portal, OpenAPI definitions or SDKs, and integrates with EHR and patient management systems through customer engagements. Research code accompanying its peer-reviewed studies (including work published in Nature Medicine) is open on GitHub.

providers.name: Radial Analytics
providers.description: Radial Analytics (Radial) is a Concord, Massachusetts healthcare technology company providing an AI/ML-powered clinical decision-support platform for the value-based care market. Its HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified software helps ACOs, hospitals, health systems, payers, and Medicare Advantage plans account for millions of clinical, claims, and quality datapoints to improve patient outcomes while reducing cost of care. Products include Radial Care, ACO Compare, Opportunity Navigator, decision-support modules, care pathways, and TEAM bundles. The company was founded by MIT PhDs Thaddeus Fulford-Jones and Eric Weiss and is backed by Initialized Capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company profile; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Siemens Healthineers
providers.description: Siemens Healthineers AG is a German medical technology company (XETRA SHL) covering medical imaging, laboratory diagnostics, point-of-care testing, advanced therapies, and cancer care (following the April 2021 Varian Medical Systems acquisition for USD 16.4 billion). Its digital surface is anchored by the teamplay digital health platform, the Digital Marketplace, syngo.via OpenApps, and the Frontier Development Kit, with developer access offered through a gated teamplay developer portal that exposes APIs for single sign-on, licensing, user roles and permissions, the teamplay receiver plug-in, DICOM image access, customer-specific report submission, and status indicator notifications. No public OpenAPI specifications are published; the API catalog and reference documentation sit behind teamplay developer account authentication.

providers.name: Tendo
providers.description: Tendo is a healthcare software company founded in 2020 by siblings Dan and Jen Goldsmith (previously of Veeva Systems and Instructure) and headquartered in the Philadelphia area. Tendo builds a cloud, purpose-built healthcare platform and a suite of applications that connect patients, clinicians, providers, and caregivers across the care journey — spanning digital patient engagement, quality and clinical documentation improvement, hospital quality rankings analytics, and the Care Connect marketplace for employers, providers, and patients. The company raised a $50M Series B led by Lux Capital (with General Catalyst). Tendo runs public trust and status surfaces (a SafeBase trust center with SOC 2 and HIPAA, an Atlassian Statuspage) but does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI; API integration is delivered under private partner agreements. Surfaced as a Lux Capital portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TytoCare
providers.description: TytoCare is an AI-powered remote physical examination and virtual care company. Its FDA-cleared handheld examination device and Home Smart Clinic / Pro Smart Clinic platforms let clinicians remotely examine heart, lungs, ears, throat, skin, and temperature, serving 240+ healthcare organizations and 1.6M+ patients. TytoCare publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs — EHR and telehealth integrations are delivered through private partner channels. An Insight Partners portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Vektor Medical
providers.description: Vektor Medical is a San Diego based medical technology company whose vMap system is an FDA-cleared and CE-marked, AI-based arrhythmia mapping solution. vMap analyzes standard 12-lead ECG data and produces beat-by-beat 2D and 3D cardiac source maps across all four chambers of the heart in about a minute, without requiring an invasive catheter-based mapping procedure. Electrophysiologists use it for triage, procedural planning and ablation guidance across focal and fibrillation-type arrhythmias and atrial and ventricular pacing. The product is delivered as Software as a Medical Device to hospitals and health systems under clinical agreements. Vektor Medical publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Virgo
providers.description: Virgo builds AI foundation models for gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy, targeting gut-mediated diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer. Its flagship model, EndoDINO, was trained on the largest known endoscopy dataset (130,037 videos / ~3.5 billion frames), and EndoML is the GI-specific tooling environment for building clinical and research workflows on top of it. Virgo Cloud provides video capture and management for endoscopy procedures, while Virgo Trials accelerates clinical trials with automatic data capture, endoscopic scoring, placebo-response prediction, subgroup identification, and AI biomarker discovery. The company was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 32 Biosciences
providers.description: 32 Biosciences (pronounced "Three Squared") is a North Chicago, Illinois gastrointestinal biotechnology company founded in 2023 that pioneers gut mucosal-immune science to prevent and treat GI disease. It emerged from stealth in September 2024 and is built on research by scientific co-founders John Alverdy MD and Eugene Chang MD of the University of Chicago and Joseph Pierre PhD of the University of Wisconsin-Madison, with Peter Farmakis as CEO. The company runs two platforms - a GI Discovery Platform that measures metabolomic signatures of gut mucosal-immune function for therapeutic discovery and clinical decision-making, and a CS Therapeutic Platform whose lead asset CS-0003 is a Mucosal Immune Modulator intended to restore and protect the GI mucosal-immune barrier across seven indications. It raised $6 million in early funding and announced a $40 million Series A launch at the 2026 J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference. 32 Biosciences publishes no product or developer API and runs no developer program; the only machine-readable surface on 32biosciences.com is the WordPress REST API (wp/v2) that serves the company newsroom, marketing and platform pages, leadership profiles, taxonomies and media library as JSON, alongside a WordPress Abilities registry that is present but authentication-gated.

providers.name: Attuned Intelligence
providers.description: Attuned Intelligence is a healthcare voice AI company that automates hospital and community health center call centers with supervised, EHR-integrated Voice AI Agents. Its agents answer every patient call instantly and in the caller's language, resolve needs end-to-end (appointment booking, medication refills, triage routing), and provide real-time human oversight with transcripts and reporting so automation stays safe and auditable. Founded in 2024 by leaders from DeepMind, Google Health, AssemblyAI, and DocuSign, the company emerged from stealth in October 2025 with $13M in funding backed by Threshold Ventures, and serves customers including Cambridge Health Alliance and Lowell Community Health Center. The platform is SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant. Attuned publishes no first-party developer/product API; its Wix-hosted marketing site exposes a generic hosted Site MCP endpoint for agentic access to public site content and business details.

providers.name: Greater Good Health
providers.description: Greater Good Health is a Manhattan Beach, California value-based senior healthcare organization founded in 2021 that delivers preventive, whole-person primary care to older adults through a nurse-practitioner-led model. It operates its own senior primary care clinics and an integrated clinical services platform — risk adjustment and annual wellness visits, transitions of care, high-risk and chronic condition management, and behavioral health — delivered on behalf of health plans, medical groups, ACOs and other risk-bearing organizations. Alongside care delivery it runs a nurse practitioner community, the Greater Good Institute education portal, and clinical technology and analytics tooling for its employed NPs. It is a care delivery organization rather than a software vendor: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Allotex
providers.description: Allotex Inc. is an ophthalmic biologics and medical device company headquartered at 27-43 Wormwood Street, Suite 160, Boston, Massachusetts, with European operations. Founded by Drs. Michael Mrochen and David Muller, it develops tissue-addition therapies for presbyopia, hyperopia and myopia. Its lead product, the Allotex TransForm corneal allograft, is a 20-micron-thick, 2.75mm-diameter disc of acellular human donor cornea shaped with an excimer laser under OCT measurement, sterilised by electron-beam radiation and shelf-stable for two years, implanted beneath a femtosecond-laser flap or on the corneal surface where it integrates with the patient's own cornea as, in the company's framing, a permanent living contact lens. Because the implant adds biocompatible human tissue rather than ablating tissue or inserting a synthetic inlay, the company positions the procedure as removable and replaceable. Allotex has run TransForm clinical trials for hyperopia and for intrastromal and sub-epithelial presbyopia correction, submitted an IDE to the U.S. FDA in May 2025 for its Allo-1 corneal implant, received FDA IDE approval for a U.S. presbyopia study in January 2026, and partners with Daicel High Performance Polymers and its TOPAS Advanced Polymers business on next-generation allograft technology. Allotex runs no developer program and publishes no product API, no developer portal, no API reference, no SDKs and no status page. The only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind us.allotex.com, catalogued here.

providers.name: BestDoc
providers.description: BestDoc is a healthcare patient-relationship-management (PRM) company that helps hospitals improve the patient experience across inpatient and outpatient care. Its platform includes BestDoc Concierge for inpatient experience management (non-clinical requests, room food ordering, discharge management), BestDoc Practice for outpatient patient-request management, BestDoc Survey for omni-channel patient feedback, an AI Reply Assistant for automated review responses, and continued-care engagement tools. BestDoc integrates with hospital information systems (HIS), EMRs, and payment gateways. BestDoc Technology Pvt. Ltd. is an ISO 27001:2013 certified company operating from Kochi, Bangalore, and Dubai. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Biostate AI
providers.description: Biostate AI is a Houston-based precision-health biotechnology company combining proprietary wet-lab chemistry with generative AI to make RNA and DNA sequencing dramatically cheaper and more accessible. Its BIRT (Barcode-Integrated Reverse Transcription) plus PERD (Probes for Excess RNA Depletion) platform delivers Total RNA sequencing from around $60 per sample, and its N-Act and RNAstate AI models turn omics data into clinical insights for autoimmune, cardiovascular, and cancer diagnostics. The company operates a cloud data lake for AI-ready omics data and runs research partnerships across the U.S., India, and China. As of this profile Biostate publishes a marketing and publications site plus open research model repositories on GitHub, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK client library, or developer portal.

providers.name: Cognoa
providers.description: Cognoa is a pediatric behavioral health company in Palo Alto, California building digital diagnostics and therapeutics for early childhood development, starting with autism. Its flagship product, Canvas Dx, is an FDA-authorized Software as a Medical Device that aids clinicians in diagnosing or ruling out autism spectrum disorder in children aged 18 to 72 months, combining a caregiver questionnaire, short home videos scored by credentialed human video analysts, and a healthcare-provider questionnaire into a machine-learning classifier that returns Positive, Negative, or Indeterminate. Canvas Dx is delivered as an iOS/Android caregiver app plus a prescriber web portal at app.cognoa.com; Cognoa ships no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: EDDA Technology
providers.description: EDDA Technology, Inc. is a Princeton, New Jersey medical imaging software company behind the IQQA platform for computer-assisted radiology and surgery. IQQA delivers 3D quantitative image analysis, automated segmentation and volumetric measurement over CT and MR studies, supporting pre-surgical planning and simulation, intra-operative guidance and monitoring, post-operative follow-up evaluation, and clinical training across liver, lung, kidney and interventional oncology. Products include IQQA-BodyImaging, IQQA-Guide, IQQA-Chest, IQQA-Liver, IQQA-Liver Function, IQQA-eQMR and the IQQA-eFusion edge-AI surgical navigation system. The company is FDA cleared and CE marked under EU MDR 2017/745, and raised a US$150 million round led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 with OrbiMed participation in April 2021. EDDA publishes no developer API for IQQA — it is regulated medical device software deployed on-premises in hospitals — so the only public API surface catalogued here is the WordPress REST API serving eddatech.com content.

providers.name: Genalyte
providers.description: Genalyte, Inc. is a San Diego, California in-vitro diagnostics company building point-of-care blood testing systems based on silicon photonic microring resonator technology. Founded by Cary Gunn, the company developed the Maverick Diagnostic System and its successor Merlin, an automated benchtop analyzer that runs hematology, chemistry and immunoassay panels — including CBC, lipid panel and comprehensive metabolic panel — from small whole-blood or serum volumes and returns results in roughly twenty to thirty minutes while the patient is still in the clinic. A cloud verification layer the company markets as CloudLab quality-checks results and routes them into electronic medical record systems. Genalyte received FDA clearance for a thyroid stimulating hormone immunoassay performed on a silicon chip and previously held an FDA Emergency Use Authorization for a rapid COVID-19 antibody test. The company is investor-backed (Khosla Ventures, Verily Life Sciences and others) and is a HIPAA covered entity that publishes a Notice of Privacy Practices. As of this profile Genalyte publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Insightec
providers.description: Insightec Ltd. is an Israeli medical device company, founded in 1999 and headquartered in Tirat Carmel, Israel, that develops and sells MR-guided focused ultrasound (MRgFUS) systems under the Exablate brand. Its Exablate Neuro platform focuses more than a thousand ultrasound beams through the intact skull to ablate a target deep in the brain without an incision, and is approved for essential tremor and Parkinson's disease, including staged bilateral treatment. The Exablate body platform is used for uterine fibroids, palliation of bone metastases, and prostate indications, and the company runs clinical programs in blood-brain-barrier opening and glioblastoma. Insightec publishes a public product documentation portal of operator manuals and handbooks for the Exablate systems, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, SDKs, or agent surface; its systems integrate with GE and Siemens MR scanners as clinical devices rather than through a public API.

providers.name: AccessHope
providers.description: AccessHope is a Los Angeles-area health benefits company, founded in 2019 and wholly owned by City of Hope, that delivers remote cancer expertise as an employer-sponsored benefit. Its subspecialist teams review a member's pathology, imaging, molecular testing and treatment plan against the latest evidence from a coalition of National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers — City of Hope, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Emory Winship, Fred Hutch, Johns Hopkins Kimmel, Northwestern Medicine Lurie, and UT Southwestern Simmons — and return guidance to the member's own local oncologist rather than moving the patient. AccessHope reports roughly 9 million covered members across 700+ employer and health-plan clients, including 70+ Fortune 500 companies. Delivery is business-to-business: employers, benefits consultants, health plans and navigation partners onboard through an eligibility file feed and an implementation-managed workflow, while members and clinical staff use credentialed web portals. AccessHope publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Ambiq Micro
providers.description: Ambiq Micro is a semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power System-on-Chip (SoC) solutions for battery-powered and endpoint-AI devices. Its proprietary Subthreshold Power Optimized Technology (SPOT) platform lets its Apollo family of Arm Cortex-M microcontrollers and Artasie real-time clocks run at extremely low energy, powering wearables, hearables, healthcare, smart-home, industrial and gaming devices. Ambiq's developer surface is an embedded C/C++ toolchain - the AmbiqSuite SDK and the open-source neuralSPOT AI SDK/Toolkit - plus a set of first-party Python AI toolkits (heartKIT, sleepKIT, physioKIT, neuralspotx) published on PyPI and GitHub (AmbiqAI, AmbiqMicro). This is not a web/REST API provider; it is profiled here for its open-source developer and AI SDK footprint.

providers.name: Dialogue
providers.description: Dialogue is a leading Canadian virtual healthcare and employee wellness provider operating an Integrated Health Platform that delivers primary care, mental health support, Employee Assistance Programs (EAP), and wellness programming to members through a single mobile and web application available 24/7/365. The company serves more than 52,000 Canadian organizations — including Sun Life, National Bank of Canada, Via Rail, Lightspeed, and Samsung — connecting employees and their families with multidisciplinary care teams of nurses, physicians, and mental health specialists. Dialogue is a consumer-facing digital health application; it does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Agilemd
providers.description: AgileMD is a clinical decision support company that embeds real-time predictive analytics and evidence-based clinical pathways directly into hospital electronic health record (EHR) workflows such as Epic and Cerner. Its FDA-cleared eCART Clinical Deterioration Suite continuously scores patient risk from nearly 100 real-time variables — labs, vital signs, and nursing assessments — to help care teams recognize deteriorating patients earlier, while its Clinical Pathways product standardizes evidence-based order sets, documentation, and protocols across care settings. AgileMD is used across 400+ hospitals by more than 150,000 clinical users and has processed millions of patient encounters. The company is backed by Y Combinator, MATTER, and Rock Health.

providers.name: DigiLens
providers.description: DigiLens Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California company that designs and manufactures holographic waveguide optics and augmented reality display systems for extended reality (XR). Its Crystal Waveguides are produced with a proprietary photopolymer material set, inkjet printing and a holographic contact-copy process rather than etching, and are supplied to partners including Samsung, Corning, Panasonic, Sony, Continental, Mitsubishi Chemical and Goertek for smartglasses, automotive head-up displays, smart helmets and avionics head-up guidance. DigiLens also ships ARGO, a standalone, rugged enterprise AR headset running DigiOS — an Android-based operating system with voice UI, gaze and scroll-wheel interaction, projector control and Microsoft Intune MDM certification. Developers build for ARGO in Unity or Android Studio on top of the DigiOS SDK and Qualcomm Snapdragon Spaces, with samples published in the digilens-ar GitHub organization and documentation on the DigiLens developer portal. DigiLens has raised a Series D led by Samsung Electronics at a valuation above $500M.

providers.name: Imagen
providers.description: Imagen (Imagen Technologies) is an AI-enabled, sub-specialized diagnostic imaging partner for independent practices, hospitals, and health systems. It combines in-clinic imaging equipment, FDA-cleared AI algorithms, and a 24/7 teleradiology network of fellowship-trained, board-certified specialists to deliver rapid, accurate radiology interpretations, plus advanced analytics for care-gap identification. Imagen operates across 23 states, serving roughly 3.5 million patients, and is backed by GV and Threshold Ventures. The company publishes a security program covering SOC 2 Type II, the HITRUST CSF, and HIPAA. Imagen Technologies exposes no public developer API surface at this time. (Note the distinct namesake company Imagen AI, imagen-ai.com, an AI photo-editing product that does publish an API and SDK.)

providers.name: Petfolk
providers.description: Petfolk is a Charlotte, North Carolina based veterinary care company that operates a network of modern, company-owned pet care centers across the US Southeast and Texas, paired with a consumer mobile app. Founded and led by veterinarian Dr. Audrey Wystrach, Petfolk provides primary and wellness care, sick and urgent care, dentistry, surgery, spay and neuter, vaccinations and diagnostics for dogs and cats, delivered under a "gentle handling" clinical model with seven-day-a-week hours and published, transparent pricing. The Petfolk iOS and Android app lets pet parents book in-person or virtual appointments, message their care team around the clock, request medications and access their pet's medical records; a paid PetfolkCare membership layers on 24/7 veterinary support and per-visit savings. The company raised a $40M Series B in October 2023 led by Movendo Capital, with White Star Capital and Idea Farm Ventures participating. Petfolk is a consumer veterinary services operator, not an API provider: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/GraphQL contract, SDKs or MCP server. It does publish a hand-authored llms.txt at the site root, which is the company's only machine-readable, agent-facing surface.

providers.name: TwinStrand Biosciences
providers.description: TwinStrand Biosciences is a Seattle, Washington genomics company founded in 2015 by Jesse Salk and Michael Schmitt that develops and commercializes Duplex Sequencing, an error-corrected next-generation-sequencing chemistry licensed from the University of Washington that independently tracks both strands of an individual DNA molecule and compares them, cutting sequencing error rates from roughly 1-in-100 to below 1-in-10,000,000 per nucleotide and making ultra-rare mutations detectable. The company sells DuplexSeq assay kits — a Mutagenesis Assay for genetic toxicology in human, rat and mouse models, an AML MRD Assay for minimal residual disease in acute myeloid leukemia, and a customizable assay — each paired with a proprietary cloud analysis pipeline that turns raw Illumina reads into duplex-consensus sequences, variant calls, mutation frequency, SBS spectra and assay quality metrics. That analysis software is not a public API: it is hosted on the DNAnexus platform and reachable only by customers through a DNAnexus project. TwinStrand publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or Postman artifact of its own, and the api., docs. and developer. subdomains of twinstrandbio.com do not resolve. The only machine-readable surface on twinstrandbio.com is the WordPress REST API at /wp-json — 349 routes across 18 namespaces — whose wp/v2 content collections are anonymously readable and serve the company publication index, patent estate, conference posters, news releases, events, team profiles, pages and media library as JSON. Its public code lives in the github.com/twinstrandbio organization, which holds a single reference-data repository and no client libraries. The DuplexSeq Mutagenesis Assay business has since been transferred to Scantox, and Exact Sciences holds an exclusive license to the Duplex Sequencing technology.

providers.name: Unmind
providers.description: Unmind is a workplace mental health platform that supports employees, develops leaders, and strengthens organisational performance through therapy, coaching, manager training, crisis care, an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), wellbeing content, insights and assessments, and Nova, an AI wellbeing coach. Customers include Uber, MLB, Samsung, British Airways, Diageo, and the NHS. Unmind publishes no public developer API; api.unmind.com is a private Apollo GraphQL backend serving its own apps.

providers.name: 7 Cups
providers.description: 7 Cups (7cups.com) is an on-demand emotional health and online therapy service founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator. It connects people seeking support with a network of trained volunteer listeners for free, anonymous one-on-one chat, and matches members with licensed therapists and social workers for paid online therapy delivered by messaging, audio, or video. The platform also runs peer community forums, group support chat rooms, and self-help "growth path" content. 7 Cups operates across 189 countries in 140 languages with hundreds of thousands of trained listeners. It is a consumer web and mobile product rather than an API-first developer platform; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and carries no public API at this time.

providers.name: Dedalus
providers.description: Dedalus Group is a European healthcare and diagnostics software provider headquartered in Florence, Italy, supplying clinical information systems, electronic patient records, laboratory and diagnostic imaging software to hospitals, laboratories and care networks across roughly 40 countries. Its product estate includes the ORBIS and ORBIS U electronic patient record suites, the Lorenzo EPR in the UK, X1.V1 in Italy, and DC4H (Digital Connect 4 Health) / Open Health Connect, an HL7 FHIR-based interoperability and longitudinal-patient-record platform the company markets under an "API economy" model. Dedalus states that DC4H exposes an FHIR API management component that third-party developers can build against, and the company participates in the openEHR community, but as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or FHIR CapabilityStatement, and no sandbox on any dedalus.com host — integration access runs through a sales and customer-support motion rather than a self-serve developer surface.

providers.name: Machinify
providers.description: Machinify is an AI-powered healthcare payment integrity platform that streamlines and automates payment processes for health plans. Its products - Coordinate (claims coordination), Subrogate (subrogation management), Audit (payment audit), Pay (payment processing), and Pharmacy (pharmacy payment integrity) - run on a unified data layer that combines claims and medical records, healthcare foundation models trained on billions of data points, and task-specific AI agents with continuous-improvement feedback loops. Machinify reports 85+ customers including 18 of the top 20 US health plans, coverage of 270 million member lives, and more than $6B in annual cost avoidance and recoveries. The company is backed by Battery Ventures and GV. Machinify does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API reference.

providers.name: MPIRIQ
providers.description: MPIRIQ (MPiriQ Science Technologies GmbH) is a Munich-based healthcare software company that automates clinical documentation for medical practices and study centers. Its AI platform structures patient data directly inside existing EMR/PMS systems, runs quality and billing validation checks in the background, and connects real-world care data to clinical research through decentralized, GDPR-compliant pseudonymization. The platform helps practices participate in clinical trials via automated indication screening and patient recruitment, giving physicians time back while opening a research revenue stream. Founded in 2024 and backed by HV Capital and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Nutritics
providers.description: Nutritics provides a real-time food and nutrition data API offering access to over one million foods (generic, branded, and recipes), up to 258 nutrient parameters, allergen data, and regional compliance options across the EU, US, Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa.

providers.name: Accurx
providers.description: Accurx is a United Kingdom clinical communication and workflow company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in London, whose software is used across NHS primary care, secondary care, and community and mental health services to message patients, run patient triage, batch-message cohorts, book and remind appointments, and (via its Scribe product) draft clinical notes with AI. Accurx integrates around the NHS as an assured IM1 live supplier, using NHS Digital's interoperability standards for primary care and connecting bi-directionally to the GP clinical-system duopoly (EMIS Health, TPP SystmOne) and Vision, plus NHS national services including the Personal Demographics Service (PDS), NHS Single Sign-On, NHS Login, and the NHS App. Accurx is a consumer and integrator of NHS FHIR and IM1 interfaces rather than a publisher of its own public developer API: as of this review it operates no public developer portal, no self-serve REST/FHIR API, and no downloadable OpenAPI or FHIR CapabilityStatement. Third-party and trust integrations are arranged through its partnerships and integration teams under partner agreement.

providers.name: Care GP
providers.description: Care GP is a Sydney-based healthcare technology company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building a suite of AI agents that automate the administrative and operational work of Australian general practice clinics. Its products include Samantha (medical document allocation that files inbound emails, faxes, and scans), Veronica (24/7 inbound and outbound phone and booking management), and a Billing beta for billing and debt-collection automation. Care GP states it is ISO 27001 certified with onshore Australian data storage, multi-factor authentication, and encryption, and reports serving 400+ clinic operators. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a customer web application (agent.caregp.com.au) but no public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI definition.

providers.name: Nines
providers.description: Nines was a teleradiology and medical-imaging AI startup founded in 2017 and backed by Accel and 8VC (a $16.5M Series A in 2019), co-founded by CEO David Stavens. It built FDA-cleared AI algorithms — NinesAI Emergent Triage (for intracranial hemorrhage and mass effect) and NinesMeasure (a lung-nodule algorithm) — alongside a live teleradiology practice. On 2022-02-18, Sirona Medical acquired Nines' AI technology, clinical data pipeline, machine-learning engines, and key personnel, folding the FDA-cleared devices into RadOS, Sirona's cloud-native Radiology Operating System (reporter, viewer, PACS, worklist, and platform AI). The nines.com domain now redirects to sironamedical.com. There is no public developer API today; a RadOS "Amplify" SDK (TypeScript/Python, REST + streaming APIs, event subscriptions) is on Sirona's roadmap as an early-access program for design partners.

providers.name: NutriDataX
providers.description: NutriDataX provides AI‑powered nutrition data services, including recipe analysis, meal‑plan generation, ingredient breakdowns, and food‑intelligence tools for both home cooks and professional developers. Their platform offers eight distinct APIs covering nutrition analysis, ingredient search, diet recommendations, grocery list creation, food‑label parsing, recipe suggestions, meal‑planning optimization, and health‑impact scoring, all accessible via REST with robust authentication and rate‑limit controls.

providers.name: Sage Care
providers.description: Sage Care (sagecare.ai) builds an AI-native, HIPAA-compliant software platform made exclusively for home care agencies. Its product bundles an AI receptionist, a purpose-built CRM, an AI notetaker and a clinical scribe that automate the intake, referral, scheduling and documentation work that home care operators handle every day. Sage Care integrates with existing home care management systems such as WellSky and AxisCare rather than replacing them, and ships native iOS and desktop applications for caregivers and office staff. The company is backed by General Catalyst and surfaced through its portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Sage Care publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation — it is an application vendor rather than an API provider, so this profile captures company identity and security/compliance posture only.

providers.name: Swift Medical
providers.description: Swift Medical develops AI-powered wound and skin care management software for healthcare organizations across acute, post-acute, home health, and hospice settings. Its flagship Skin & Wound app captures calibrated wound images on mobile devices, applies computer-vision tissue analytics and auto-tracing to measure and classify wounds, and coordinates care through longitudinal documentation backed by the company's database of more than 32 million wound images. The platform emphasizes secure, compliant handling of protected health information (SOC 2 Type 2, encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, MFA) and single sign-on via Okta and Microsoft. Swift Medical does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is handled through direct engagement and enterprise SSO/EHR arrangements. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Tomorrow Health
providers.description: Tomorrow Health is an AI-powered platform for home-based care that connects providers, payors, and durable medical equipment (DMEPOS) suppliers, using intelligent automation to simplify ordering, routing, and reviewing home healthcare services. Its Horizon Suite includes AI Ordering, AI Fax Intake, and THEA (Tomorrow Health Expert Assistant). Headquartered in New York and backed by a16z, Bond Capital, and Obvious Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or API documentation is currently published; the customer application is a private authenticated web app.

providers.name: 4baseCare
providers.description: 4baseCare is a precision oncology company founded in 2018, headquartered in Bengaluru, India with operations in Singapore, that combines next-generation-sequencing comprehensive genomic profiling with AI-driven clinical decision support to personalize cancer treatment. Its portfolio spans the TARGT family of tissue, liquid-biopsy and dual-source (SoLiQ) panels, germline and HRD testing, the OncoTwin AI insights layer, a Global Cancer Diversity Atlas of 30,000+ genomic profiles, molecular tumor board support, and the Oncobuddy patient program. Clinical results and decision support are delivered to oncologists through the Galens web portal at galens.4basecare.com. The company is Illumina Accelerator backed and closed a Series B round in 2024. As of the 2026-09-05 probe it publishes no developer program, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract; the only API-shaped host, api.4basecare.com, is the private CodeIgniter application backend behind the Galens single-page app.

providers.name: Caliber Fitness
providers.description: Caliber Fitness, Inc. is a consumer strength-training and fitness-coaching company behind the Caliber: Strength Training app (iOS and Android). Caliber combines data-driven resistance-training and nutrition programming, a library of 600+ exercises, workout tracking, and one-on-one video coaching from certified personal trainers across free, Caliber Plus, and Premium Coaching tiers. Founded by Justin Fauci and Chris Muir, the company is backed by Trinity Ventures. Caliber operates as a consumer mobile app and coaching service; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time. This profile tracks its public web, legal, and membership surface within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Evidation Health
providers.description: Evidation Health is a San Mateo, California digital health company, founded in 2012, that measures health in everyday life and runs permissioned real-world data research at scale. Its consumer app and platform — Achievement — rewards members for connecting wearables, apps and health records, and its enterprise Research & Engagement Platform gives life-sciences, payer, government and non-profit customers eConsent and onboarding, ePRO and survey capture, passive and active device monitoring, program analytics, and participant education. Evidation combines data from sources including Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Dexcom and EHR/claims records (via a partnership with 1upHealth's FHIR-based Patient Connect, and with HealthVerity), and has enabled 175+ virtual real-world studies and 70+ peer-reviewed publications. Evidation publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surfaces are the member app backend and enterprise data deliveries, neither of which is publicly documented.

providers.name: Headspace
providers.description: Headspace is a global mental health platform offering consumer mindfulness, meditation, and sleep content alongside Headspace Care (formerly Ginger) — on-demand coaching, therapy, and psychiatry — and Headspace EAP. The B2B business (Headspace for Organizations) serves 4,000+ employers, health plans, and consultants in 190+ countries with a stratified care model (AI companion Ebb, coaches, therapists, psychiatrists). Integration surfaces for enterprise customers — eligibility file feeds, SSO, SCIM, benefit-platform connectors — are delivered under enterprise contracts and are not exposed via a public developer portal. There is no public REST API, no published OpenAPI specification, and no self-serve partner onboarding.

providers.name: Midi Health
providers.description: Midi Health is a virtual care platform for women in midlife, delivering insurance-covered telemedicine from clinicians who specialize in perimenopause, menopause, and related midlife health. Patients get personalized care plans spanning hormone therapy (HRT), GLP-1 and weight management, sexual wellness, mood, sleep, hair and skin, and cancer-survivorship care, plus prescriptions, compounded medications, and supplements, with coverage available across all 50 states. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Midi operates as a direct-to-consumer and employer/health-plan telehealth service. No public API, developer portal, or technical developer surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: 10x Genomics
providers.description: 10x Genomics is a life sciences technology company building instruments, reagents, and software that resolve biology at single-cell and spatial resolution. Its Chromium platform delivers single-cell gene expression, immune profiling, and multiomic analysis; its Visium and Xenium platforms deliver spatial transcriptomics and in situ single-cell spatial biology. The company supports researchers with analysis software (Cell Ranger, Space Ranger, Xenium Onboard Analysis, Loupe Browser), a cloud analysis platform, and open datasets. 10x Genomics does not publish a general-purpose public REST developer API; its developer surface is command-line analysis pipelines, file-format tooling, and open-source repositories on GitHub.

providers.name: Apero
providers.description: Apero Health is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed healthcare technology company that provides an integrated practice-management and revenue-cycle-management (RCM) platform for medical practices. Its cloud software unifies scheduling, clinical visit notes, insurance eligibility verification and claims billing, patient billing and payments, e-prescriptions, and financial reporting, and claims to reduce billing time by up to 80% while helping practices scale operations. Apero exposes a fully-featured REST API, webhooks, and CSV import that connect healthcare and finance workflows, and integrates with payers (Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield) and platforms including Stripe, QuickBooks Online, Google, and Snowflake.

providers.name: Bristol Myers Squibb
providers.description: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) is a global Fortune 500 biopharmaceutical company committed to discovering, developing, and delivering innovative medicines for patients with serious diseases. BMS focuses on oncology, immunology, cardiovascular, fibrosis, and cell therapy (CAR T). The company operates BMS Study Connect for clinical trial recruitment, a Medical Information portal for healthcare providers, and the BMS Business Development platform for research partnerships and data sharing. BMS actively pursues technology partnerships in protein degradation, advanced treatment modalities, and digital health.

providers.name: Dandy
providers.description: Dandy is a digital dental lab platform for dentists, dental practices, and dental service organizations (DSOs). It combines intraoral scanner hardware, cloud-based case management software, and in-house dental lab manufacturing into a single scan-to-lab workflow. Dentists capture digital impressions with a Dandy intraoral scanner, submit cases through Dandy software, collaborate in real time with lab technicians via chat, video, and chairside scan review, and receive finished restorations manufactured by Dandy. Product lines include crowns, bridges, implants, clear aligners, retainers, dentures, night guards, splints, and sleep apnea devices. Dandy positions itself as an AI-powered digital dental lab modernizing restorative and orthodontic dentistry. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes an agent-facing llms.txt and ai-index.json but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Disclo
providers.description: Disclo is a workplace-accommodations software platform that powers end-to-end management of ADA, FMLA, and state-leave requests, medical-certification verification, and the interactive accommodation process for employers. The HIPAA- and SOC 2-compliant portal automates accommodation workflows and compliance documentation, adds AI-assisted medical-certification review (Disclo Verify) and candidate accommodations for recruiting (Disclo Hire), and integrates with 50+ HRIS and ATS systems. Disclo is a private B2B SaaS company backed by Bain Capital Ventures and General Catalyst; it operates a secure customer portal (secure.disclo.com) and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI. Access is enterprise, demo/sales-led rather than self-serve.

providers.name: ianacare
providers.description: ianacare ("iana" = I Am Not Alone) is a Boston-based caregiver support and navigation platform that sells to employers, health plans and providers as a benefit for the working family caregivers in their populations. Founded in 2018 by Jessica Kim and Steven Lee, it pairs a consumer mobile app — where a caregiver mobilizes an informal care team, coordinates practical tasks, unlocks employer benefits and finds local resources — with human Caregiver Navigators, and positions itself as a partner for fulfilling CMS GUIDE Model dementia-care requirements. The company raised a $12.1M Series A in January 2022 led by Greycroft with 8VC, SemperVirens, Able Partners and the Brown Angel Group. ianacare ships software only as an end-user product: the iOS and Android apps and the app.ianacare.com web client are backed by first-party hosts (iana.ianacare.com behind a JWT bearer token, api.ianacare.com behind a CloudFront 403) and by ianacare's own Auth0 custom domain auth.ianacare.com, which is the single machine-readable contract the company publishes. There is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, CLI, webhook catalog, MCP server or agent card on any ianacare host.

providers.name: Opalite Health
providers.description: Opalite Health is building the language layer for healthcare. Its platform delivers real-time, AI-powered medical interpretation across 150+ languages, validated against certified human interpreters and engineered for HIPAA-aligned, clinical-grade use. Opalite connects providers and patients with limited English proficiency in seconds — through EHR workflows and rapid healthcare deployment — to close language gaps that drive health inequities and poor outcomes. The company publishes a marketing and validation-study presence but does not operate a public developer API program; api.opalitehealth.com is a private application backend. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched with the company's real identity, compliance posture (HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, AES-256 encryption), and domain-security probes.

providers.name: Cleerly
providers.description: Cleerly is a digital healthcare company building an AI-powered platform for the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease (heart disease). Its software analyzes coronary CT angiography (CCTA) imaging to automatically quantify and characterize atherosclerotic plaque, measure stenosis severity, and stage disease, giving physicians a precise, personalized picture of a patient's heart-disease risk. The goal is to move heart-disease care from symptom-based testing toward direct measurement of plaque, reducing unnecessary invasive procedures while improving diagnostic accuracy. Cleerly operates as an enterprise clinical SaaS delivered to health systems, cardiologists, and imaging centers rather than a public developer API program; it publishes a marketing and clinical-evidence site plus a clinician-facing application (Cleerly Labs) and a public trust center. Cleerly is backed by Battery Ventures and Insight Partners.

providers.name: Floy
providers.description: Floy is a Munich-based healthcare AI company (founded 2021) that builds AI-powered radiology software for medical imaging. Its two products — opportunistic screening and diagnostic assistance — analyse CT and MRI examinations to surface additional findings beyond the initial radiologist assessment, enabling earlier diagnosis and better patient outcomes. The models are trained on 17 million medical examinations. Floy is an ISO 13485:2016 certified, EU MDR Class IIb medical-device manufacturer and is GDPR compliant, with research partnerships including DKFZ, LMU Klinikum Munich, Stanford, and the University of Oxford. It is backed by HV Capital, 10x Founders, xdeck, and Acurio Ventures. Floy is a clinical B2B product and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Peppy
providers.description: Peppy is a global employee healthcare benefits platform, delivered through a mobile app, that connects workers with specialist clinicians across key life stages. Offered by employers as a benefit, Peppy provides unlimited access to practitioners covering women's health, men's health, fertility, pregnancy and early parenthood, menopause, and neurodiversity, alongside lifestyle support for nutrition, fitness, and mental wellbeing. Peppy operates a consumer and employer facing service and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its published web properties and security posture. Peppy is a Seedcamp portfolio company.

providers.name: Stryker
providers.description: Stryker Corporation is a Fortune 500 medical technologies company offering products in orthopedics, medical and surgical equipment, and neurotechnology and spine. Stryker provides Connected OR integration platforms and Smart Equipment Management (SEM) systems for healthcare facilities. The company does not currently offer a publicly documented developer API. Stryker's digital health products include the Mako robotic arm for orthopedic surgery, iSuite integrated OR technology, and asset tracking systems. Integration with hospital EHR and OR management systems is done through vendor partnerships rather than public APIs.

providers.name: GT Medical Technologies
providers.description: GT Medical Technologies, Inc. is a Tempe, Arizona medical device company founded by brain tumor specialists to commercialize GammaTile, an FDA-cleared, bioabsorbable collagen implant embedded with Cesium-131 radiation seeds. Surgeons place the tiles directly into the resection cavity at the time of brain tumor removal, delivering immediate, targeted radiation without the weeks-long healing delay conventional external beam radiotherapy requires. The company sells a physical, prescription-only implant to hospitals and neurosurgical centers through a direct sales force and a Salesforce-based ordering portal; it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Ultromics
providers.description: Ultromics is a UK-based clinical AI company, spun out of the University of Oxford and backed by GV, whose EchoGo platform applies FDA 510(k)-cleared AI to routine echocardiograms to help clinicians detect heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and cardiac amyloidosis. EchoGo integrates into existing hospital echo workflows and PACS environments, delivering results through clinical systems rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Virta Health
providers.description: Virta Health is a virtual, nutrition-first healthcare company delivering sustainable weight loss and type 2 diabetes reversal. Its program combines personalized nutrition plans, continuous expert health coaching, physician-led medication management, and connected devices, delivered through a consumer mobile app and sold to employers, health plans, and healthcare providers. Virta is HITRUST- and SOC 2 Type II-certified and operates as a HIPAA-covered clinical service. As of this enrichment pass Virta publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification surface; this profile captures its public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: Allara
providers.description: Allara Health is a virtual women's healthcare platform focused on complex hormonal, metabolic, and gynecological conditions such as PCOS, insulin resistance, endometriosis, thyroid disorders, menopause, and PMDD. Serving more than 85,000 patients across 45 states and D.C., Allara connects members with board-certified OB-GYNs, endocrinologists, women's health nurse practitioners, and registered dietitians for virtual consultations, advanced hormonal and metabolic lab testing, personalized treatment plans, and ongoing care coordination. The company operates consumer-facing web and patient portal applications; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as an index-ventures portfolio company.

providers.name: Aluna
providers.description: Aluna is a digital respiratory health company behind an FDA-cleared, portable Bluetooth spirometer and companion mobile app that let people with asthma, COPD, and cystic fibrosis measure lung function (FEV1) at home and share the results with their care teams. The platform pairs a hospital-grade sensor with a gamified app and machine-learning analytics to encourage proper technique, track symptoms, triggers, and medications, and surface trends that help clinicians intervene before an exacerbation. Founded by Charvi Shetty and Inderjit Jutla out of UC Berkeley's bioengineering program, Aluna raised a $15.3M Series B and is a Matrix Partners portfolio company; the product is now operated under Huma Therapeutics. Aluna publishes consumer, clinical-provider, and clinical-trial surfaces but no public developer API.

providers.name: Big Sky Health
providers.description: Big Sky Health (now operating as Zero Longevity Science, Inc.) is a Bozeman, Montana consumer digital-health company best known for Zero, one of the most popular intermittent-fasting and nutrition-tracking mobile apps. Zero combines a fasting timer, photo-based meal and protein logging, a personalized Protein Score, and water-intake tracking to help users manage body composition and adopt science-backed longevity practices. The company runs as a direct-to-consumer mobile subscription business (Zero Plus) on iOS and Android. As of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer program. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Trinity Ventures portfolio company awaiting enrichment.

providers.name: Birches Health
providers.description: Birches Health is a fully virtual behavioral addiction treatment provider specializing in gambling disorder and related compulsive behaviors such as sports betting, day trading, video gaming, and pornography. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, the company delivers confidential online care from licensed gambling counselors, peer mentors, financial coaches, and group therapy across all 50 states. Birches Health partners with 18+ state governments that have legalized sports betting and 100+ national insurance plans (including UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Aetna, and Blue Cross Blue Shield) so most clients pay $0-25 per session, with a core program completed in about 12 weeks. The company has raised approximately $20M from AlleyCorp, General Catalyst, and Will Ventures. Birches Health does not currently publish a public developer API, portal, or specification; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Caer
providers.description: Caer, Inc. is the company behind YUMI (helloyumi.com), a direct-to-consumer children's nutrition brand that makes nutritionally-engineered organic snacks for babies, toddlers, and kids. The product line includes toddler bars, squeezable smoothies-to-go, freeze-dried smoothie melts, super/breakfast bars, and soft-baked cookies, all formulated as function-first, nutrient-dense, organic, dairy-free, gluten-free, and clean-label. YUMI sells through its own WooCommerce storefront, Amazon, and select retail, offering one-time purchases and recurring subscription memberships. Backed by 500 Global. This profile was seeded as a venture-portfolio stub; it is a consumer packaged-goods e-commerce brand with no first-party public developer API, so most API-artifact scoring dimensions are not applicable.

providers.name: Floreo
providers.description: Floreo is a research-based virtual reality (VR) digital therapeutics company that delivers immersive lessons teaching social, behavioral, communication, and life skills to neurodiverse individuals, including autistic children and adults. The platform runs across mobile (iPhone with Google Cardboard) and standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2/3/Pro, PICO), with a companion clinician portal for supervised sessions, progress tracking, and telehealth-style delivery. Floreo holds an FDA Breakthrough Device designation and participates in the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP), and works with schools, behavioral-health providers, Medicaid programs, and research partners. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Fort
providers.description: Fort is a Y Combinator (W26) hardware startup building a screenless wearable that automatically tracks strength training for people who care about longevity. Founded by three former Tesla engineers, the device uses heart rate and motion sensing to detect gym sessions, workout classes, sleep, and recovery without requiring the wearer to manually log reps, sets, or exercises, then delivers actionable feedback on how lifestyle factors affect strength progress. Fort is styled as jewelry rather than performance gear, ships in three finishes with 7+ day battery life, and pairs with Fort Foundations, an expert-led training program built around core movement patterns. The product is currently available for pre-order and has no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public web and commercial presence.

providers.name: Framewise Health
providers.description: Framewise Health is an AI-native patient engagement platform (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) that converts a patient's medical records into personalized, clinically-reviewed educational videos. The platform pulls patient data from electronic health records over any FHIR R4 endpoint, generates discharge and treatment-adherence education tailored to the individual using institutional protocols and drug-information databases, and delivers it by SMS in 75+ languages with no app and no login. It then tracks patient comprehension in real time, giving care teams engagement data to flag which patients need follow-up. Framewise integrates with Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), Athenahealth, ModMed, eClinicalWorks, and NextGen, and is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant with an AWS BAA and end-to-end encryption. It targets hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, and private clinics seeking to improve patient outcomes and medication adherence.

providers.name: Headlight
providers.description: Headlight is a US mental health services company delivering teletherapy, in-person therapy, psychiatry, and medication management through a clinician-centered care model. Founded by Drs. Manish Sheth and Shashita Inamdar, it helps patients move from initial interest to a well-matched therapist or prescriber with less friction, treating conditions including depression, anxiety, ADHD, bipolar disorder, PTSD, trauma, OCD, panic disorder, postpartum depression, and insomnia. Headlight is in-network with major insurers (Aetna, Blue Cross, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Humana, Kaiser, Moda) and operates across Alaska, California, Colorado, Oregon, Texas, and Washington. The company raised $18M led by Matrix and EPIC Ventures. This is a consumer clinical services provider with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Homage
providers.description: Homage is a Singapore-headquartered holistic health and caregiving platform that connects families with screened, professional caregivers, nurses, and therapists to deliver personal care, home nursing procedures, rehabilitation, and health services where people live. Founded in 2016, Homage operates across Singapore, Malaysia, and Australia through consumer mobile apps and a care-management operations platform, offering flexible on-demand and recurring visits, care assessments, custom care plans, and teleconsultations for conditions such as dementia, stroke recovery, and post-surgical care. Homage does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web properties and probed domain security.

providers.name: MedHOK (Hearst Communications)
providers.description: MHK (formerly MedHOK), part of Hearst Health, is a healthcare technology company providing a unified SaaS platform for health plans and payers. Its CareProminence suite spans utilization management, care management, complaints/appeals and grievances, pharmacy management, population health and quality management, and interoperability (the MHK Interop Suite), while its MarketProminence suite covers enrollment and member maintenance, premium billing, financial reconciliation, and member web portals. MHK helps Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial health plans streamline operations, ensure regulatory compliance, and improve the member experience. The MHK Interop Suite supports FHIR, SMART on FHIR, Da Vinci, and CMS-0057 interoperability requirements. MHK publishes HITRUST and ISO 27001 certification and NCQA prevalidation. The company operates a public marketing and resource site but does not publish a public developer portal or API program.

providers.name: nference
providers.description: nference is a healthcare-AI company that builds an agentic intelligence layer for clinical research and drug development. Its nSights platform aggregates and analyzes de-identified multimodal patient data at massive scale — 1.4 billion+ clinical notes, 10 billion+ radiology images, 20 million+ digitized pathology whole-slide images, 12 million+ ECG waveforms, and 100 million+ echocardiogram videos — extracting 30,000+ clinical biomarkers to help life-sciences and health-system partners design patient cohorts, explore patient journeys, annotate data for model development, and run advanced data-science workflows across cardiology, oncology, immunology, rare diseases, neurology, infectious diseases, and nephrology. nference spun out the venture companies Anumana (ECG-based biomarker discovery) and Pramana (digital pathology). The company operates as an enterprise B2B platform with no public self-serve API; it is profiled here for its security, compliance, and governance posture. Backed by Matrix Partners.

providers.name: Prenuvo
providers.description: Prenuvo operates a preventive healthcare screening service built around whole-body MRI imaging paired with blood biomarker panels and personalized results reviews. A single scan captures on the order of a billion data points while screening for hundreds of conditions across major organ systems, without radiation or contrast agents, and completes in under an hour. Blood panels measure 80+ biomarkers tied to inflammation, hormone levels, and metabolic health, with optional advanced imaging for brain, heart, and body composition. Prenuvo runs clinics across the US, Canada, Australia, and the UK, and works with research institutions including Mount Sinai, UCLA, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, and Penn. Prenuvo does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Summer Health
providers.description: Summer Health is a pediatric health company offering families fast, board-certified pediatric care. Its flagship consumer service provides comprehensive at-home blood work for children ages 8-18 (one blood draw covering 74 biomarkers) reviewed by board-certified pediatricians over video, alongside text-based urgent-care messaging with pediatric clinicians. The service is HSA/FSA eligible and LegitScript-approved. Summer Health is a consumer-facing telehealth offering and does not currently publish a public developer program, API documentation, or third-party integration surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lux Capital and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Teal Health
providers.description: Teal Health, Inc. is a women's health company behind the Teal Wand, the first and only FDA-approved at-home self-collection device for cervical cancer screening in the United States. Its end-to-end telehealth service pairs the self-collection kit with virtual Teal medical providers who prescribe the kit, review Roche cobas HPV lab results, and support patients aged 25-65 throughout the screening experience. Now available in all 50 states, Teal Health runs a HIPAA-compliant direct-to-consumer telehealth platform and is a consumer of third-party healthcare APIs (Healthie for scheduling/telehealth, Candid for billing) rather than a publisher of a public developer API.

providers.name: Cadence Solutions
providers.description: Cadence Solutions, Inc. — operating as Cadence — is a New York-based clinical AI and remote patient monitoring company founded in 2020 by Chris Altchek. Cadence partners with large health systems and payers to deliver continuous chronic-care management between clinic visits: FDA-cleared connected devices (blood pressure cuffs, glucometers, weight scales) stream daily vitals to a 24/7 clinical care team backed by supervised AI agents that flag out-of-range readings, close care gaps, and escalate to clinicians for medication titration. The platform covers hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure and COPD, is integrated two-way into partner EHRs (Epic, Oracle Cerner, athenahealth), and supports Medicare RPM/CCM and the CMS ACCESS model. Cadence serves more than 100,000 patients across systems including Community Health Systems, LifePoint Health, Providence, Rush, MemorialCare, Corewell Health, Ardent Health and Duke Health. It raised a $100M Series C led by Spark Capital in June 2026 ($241M total, ~$1.23B valuation). Cadence publishes no public developer program or API: EHR interoperability is delivered as bilateral health system integrations, not a self-serve API surface.

providers.name: Curevo
