providers.description: Curevo is a clinical‑stage biotechnology company that operates a global healthcare marketplace, connecting patients with verified medical centers, doctors, and wellness providers across more than 150 countries. The platform offers a range of treatments—from cardiology and oncology to regenerative therapies such as stem cell, hyperbaric oxygen, and blood ozonation—facilitating transparent pricing, tele‑assist AI support, and end‑to‑end medical travel coordination.

providers.name: Lucis
providers.description: Lucis is a Paris-based, AI-powered preventative health platform (Y Combinator P25; backed by General Catalyst) that helps members understand their biology through comprehensive lab testing and personalised coaching. Members receive two annual lab assessments (blood, urine, and saliva) at 450+ partner labs across Europe, producing 110+ data points across 11 body systems — metabolic, cardiovascular, hormonal, nervous, and more — which an AI engine turns into personalised action plans spanning nutrition, supplementation, sleep, activity, and mental health. The platform ingests wearable data (Garmin, Withings, Oura, Strava; Apple Watch and Whoop coming soon) for ongoing monitoring. Lucis is a consumer health product; as of this profile it exposes a member web/mobile application and a compliance portal but publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Md Ally
providers.description: MD Ally is a New York-based digital health company that integrates telehealth into the 911 emergency response system. Its platform lets emergency dispatchers route low-acuity, non-emergency callers to a virtual care tier, connecting patients with telehealth clinicians, in-network resources, and social services instead of dispatching EMS or defaulting to an emergency-room visit. MD Ally works with public safety agencies and payers to expand traditional two-tier dispatch models, reduce unnecessary ambulance transports and ER visits, and improve patient navigation. Backed by General Catalyst and Techstars.

providers.name: Transcarent
providers.description: Transcarent is a health and care experience company serving self-insured employers, health plans, and government and labor union clients. Its consumer-facing platform, WayFinding, combines generative AI agents with instant access to human health guides and clinicians to deliver benefits navigation, clinical guidance, virtual primary and specialty care, pharmacy care, surgery care, cancer care, weight-health programs, and 2nd.MD second opinions in a single experience. The platform is built on an API-first, cloud-native architecture with pre-built HL7 FHIR and EDI connectors that integrate with existing eligibility files and medical, pharmacy, and point-solution benefits. Transcarent exposes these integrations to enterprise partners rather than through a public self-serve developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: Clivi
providers.description: Clivi is Mexico's largest digital clinic for diabetes and obesity care, delivering fully online telehealth treatment that combines endocrinologists, internists, nutritionists, and psychologists with continuous glucose monitoring and GLP-1 medications (Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Saxenda, Rybelsus). Founded in 2020 and based in Mexico City, Clivi serves patients nationwide through WhatsApp-based virtual care, home medication delivery via its Farmacia Clivi digital pharmacy, and tiered treatment plans (Clivi Pro, Plus, Total, and Zero). Backed by 500 Global and other investors, Clivi operates as a consumer healthtech service; it publishes no public developer API, but does expose an llms.txt content index for AI agents.

providers.name: DynamiCare Health
providers.description: DynamiCare Health provides technology solutions for substance use recovery, offering digital therapeutics, contingency management, and support tools for individuals, families, and health plans. Their platform integrates evidence‑based interventions, insurance navigation, and outcome tracking to improve recovery outcomes.

providers.name: kelaHealth
providers.description: kelaHealth is a healthcare AI company that improves surgical outcomes through its Surgical Intelligence Service, an AI-enabled API delivering patient-specific predictive insights at critical decision points across the perioperative process. Models trained on millions of surgical procedures predict individual patient risk across nine major complication categories, identify modifiable factors, and recommend stratified interventions tailored to hospital standards. The service integrates into existing medtech and healthcare software applications using EHR, robotic, and social-determinants-of-health data to help providers improve growth, efficiency, quality, and safety. kelaHealth is HIPAA compliant and backed by Techstars. It does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; its API is delivered through partner integrations.

providers.name: NutriSense
providers.description: NutriSense is a metabolic health and wellness company that pairs continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) with 1:1 registered-dietitian coaching and a mobile app. Members receive glucose biosensors, real-time and historical glucose analytics, AI-assisted pattern insights, stress-management sessions, and video consults with credentialed, glucose-certified nutritionists to build sustainable nutrition, weight-loss, and metabolic-health habits. Nutrisense runs a consumer product with a member web and mobile app experience; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. It does publish a machine-readable llms.txt at nutrisense.io/llms.txt.

providers.name: Prax Health
providers.description: Prax Health is a healthcare platform that helps nurse practitioners launch and grow their own independent practices. It provides an all-in-one back office that handles business formation, regulatory and clinical compliance, medical billing, insurance credentialing, an integrated EHR, and ongoing practice consulting. The company's stated mission is to put healthcare back in the hands of providers by removing the administrative and operational burden that keeps clinicians from practicing independently. Prax Health is a venture-backed company (Canaan Partners) and operates a consumer/clinician web application rather than a public developer platform; as of this profile it exposes no public API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Unobravo
providers.description: Unobravo is Europe's largest online psychology service, founded in 2019 by psychologist Danila De Stefano. It matches people with one of 9,500+ individually vetted psychologists and psychotherapists for individual, couples, and group therapy delivered online, serving Italy, Spain, and France as well as Italians abroad, with 500,000+ people supported across more than 10 million online sessions, plus a B2B mental-wellbeing offering (Unobravo Business) and an ECM training academy. Backed by Insight Partners and Northzone. Its backend API (api.unobravo.com) is private, with no public developer surface.

providers.name: Voom Medical Devices
providers.description: Voom Medical Devices, Inc. is an orthopedic medical device and surgical innovation company founded by bunion surgeon Dr. Neal Blitz and headquartered in Brentwood, Tennessee. Voom designs implants and procedural systems for minimally invasive bunion surgery (MIBS) and foot-and-ankle reconstruction, including the patented Revcon non-compression dual-zone bone screw system, the Bunionplasty 360 Bunion Repair procedure, and the MIBS CoPilot Shift + Targeting Guide single-use sterile kit. The company sells to surgeons and hospitals, runs a surgeon training program, and operates the patient-facing Bunionplasty.com procedure site with a doctor locator. It is a physical device manufacturer: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Blackrock Neurotech
providers.description: Blackrock Neurotech is a Salt Lake City, Utah based neurotechnology company that designs and manufactures implantable brain-computer interface (BCI) systems and the research instrumentation around them. Its platform pairs Utah Array microelectrode arrays and the next-generation Neuralace interface with the NeuroPort, Cerebus and CerePlex Direct neural signal processors, the CereStim stimulation system, and the Central software suite for acquisition, visualization and offline spike sorting. The company reports more than 19 years of human clinical study, 1,000+ research institutions served and 2,000+ published studies using its hardware. Blackrock does not publish a public web API: its programmatic surface is a set of device and file-format libraries distributed as downloads and GitHub source (cbSDK C++ API, cbMEX MATLAB API, CereStim API, brPY/brpylib Python data loader, and the NPMK MATLAB toolkit). Enrichment probing on 2026-08-02 found no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP, agent card, llms.txt or /.well-known/ discovery surface on any Blackrock host.

providers.name: Cleardata
providers.description: ClearDATA is healthcare's dedicated cloud security, compliance, and operations partner, helping providers, payers, health-tech software companies, medical device makers, and life sciences organizations build and run on AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud in a HIPAA- and HITRUST-aligned way. Its offering spans Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) with 300+ healthcare-specific safeguards, Managed Detection & Response (MDR), automated Cloud Compliance, and Cloud Operations, delivered through the CyberHealth platform and managed/professional services. ClearDATA is an AWS Level 1 MSSP and Microsoft Gold Partner, and maps controls to HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, NIST, ISO, PCI, and GDPR. ClearDATA is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; ClearDATA does not publish a public developer API or portal.

providers.name: DayDream Dental
providers.description: DayDream Dental is a full-service dental billing and revenue cycle management (RCM) provider that runs the insurance and billing operations for dental practices and DSOs so clinical teams can focus on patient care. Services span insurance verification with custom coding breakdowns saved directly to the practice management system (PMS), clean claims submission with attachments and narratives, payment posting with accurate insurance adjustments, diligent claim follow-up every seven days until paid with denials appealed, and patient billing via text, email, and mail. DayDream operates a HIPAA-focused trust center and a client dashboard app, and publishes a blog, CDT-code and payer references, videos, and demo scheduling for onboarding new offices. This is a service company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Illumix
providers.description: Illumix is an enterprise-grade spatial AI company spun out of Stanford's Computer Science Department, providing a core stack for real-world location intelligence that runs at the edge with centimeter-level precision. Its hardware-agnostic platform delivers sub-second localization and 3D mapping across mobile devices, AR/VR wearables, and robotics using standard cameras — with no LiDAR or GPS dependency — combining multimodal vision-language AI with long-term memory that learns behavior over time. Illumix serves AI/XR wearables, enterprise and logistics, defense and security, location-based entertainment, and robotics, with deployments referenced for Disney, Six Flags, Cedar Fair, MGM Resorts, Warner Bros, Verizon, and Sony. The company markets developer APIs and an SDK as part of a full-stack offering, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Oviva
providers.description: Oviva is a European digital health company, founded in 2014, delivering personalized, dietitian-led care for people managing type 2 diabetes, obesity, and other diet-related conditions. It combines a mobile app for logging food, activity, and progress with human coaching from a network of 420+ dietitians, psychologists, and doctors, operating across the UK, Germany, and Switzerland and serving 900K+ people. Oviva is delivered as a regulated digital therapeutic (CE-marked, ISO 27001, NHS DTAC and CQC assessed) rather than through a public developer API; this profile captures its security, compliance, and legal surface. Backed by Partech.

providers.name: Rx Redefined
providers.description: Rx Redefined Inc is a healthcare technology company in Arroyo Grande, California, founded in 2018, that operates a patented, compliance-focused DMEPOS (durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies) platform for physicians. The platform lets a medical practice become a licensed physician-owned DMEPOS supplier and distribute medical supplies — insulin pumps, breast pumps, ostomy pouches, urinary catheters — directly to its own patients instead of handing the order to a third-party supplier. It ships two products: a Full-Service product built around physician personal performance, and an In-Office product built around the in-office ancillary services exception. The platform covers CMS licensing onboarding, electronic ordering with per-order compliance and eligibility checks, supply-chain integration with 10+ U.S. distribution centers, and end-to-end revenue-cycle and audit management. The company reports use across 350+ U.S. clinics and runs on ISO 27001 certified infrastructure with HIPAA controls. The product is a customer-only web application at app.rxredefined.com; Rx Redefined publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Viome
providers.description: Viome (Viome Life Sciences) is a health technology company founded in 2016 by Naveen Jain that uses metatranscriptomic RNA sequencing — a technique originally developed for biodefense at Los Alamos National Laboratory — combined with artificial intelligence to measure active gene expression across the gut microbiome, oral microbiome, and human cells. From at-home stool, saliva, and finger-prick blood samples the company produces over 50 health scores across eight categories (BioAge, Gut Health, Oral Health, Energy, Inflammaging, Mood/Memory/Focus, Immunity, and Heart and Metabolic Health), personalized food recommendations across more than 370 foods, and custom-blended precision supplements and biotics. Products include the Full Body Intelligence, Gut Intelligence, and Oral Health Intelligence tests plus the CancerDetect saliva screening test for oral and throat cancer. Viome operates in over 100 countries, publishes peer-reviewed research in NPJ Genomic Medicine, iScience, and Microbiome, and runs a Life Sciences research division. Viome publishes no public developer API or machine-readable API contract; its consumer app at my.viome.com is served by an undocumented private backend, and the only agent-facing artifact the company publishes is a curated llms.txt.

providers.name: Chewy
providers.description: Chewy, Inc. is a Fortune 500 American online retailer of pet food, pet products, prescription medications, and veterinary services headquartered in Plantation, Florida. Chewy is one of the largest e-commerce pet retailers in the United States and supports a customer-focused operating model centered on subscription Autoship orders, Chewy Pharmacy prescription fulfillment, Connect with a Vet telehealth, and Chewy Health insurance. Chewy provides vendor and supplier integration primarily through the Dsco supplier integration platform rather than a public consumer-facing developer API. The Dsco-based integration supports core EDI transactions for purchase orders, inventory updates, shipment confirmations, and invoices, enabling brands and third-party logistics providers to connect with Chewy's e-commerce marketplace.

providers.name: Denticon
providers.description: Denticon is a cloud-based dental practice management platform built for dental service organizations (DSOs) and multi-location group practices, owned and operated by Planet DDS (which also owns Cloud 9 Ortho and Apteryx imaging). The Denticon API program - relaunched in July 2024 on a new developer portal powered by Azure API Management - exposes RESTful APIs, webhooks, and batch data extracts covering patient, appointment, financial/ledger, insurance and claims (Revenue Cycle Management), clinical, and practice/office data, with OAuth 2.0 auth, an event-driven architecture for synchronized updates, and writebacks into Denticon. API access is partner-gated - Planet DDS must approve vendors and each client practice authorizes vendor access to specific office locations (OIDs). Public documentation exists, but keys and interactive access require program enrollment, so the endpoint surface below is modeled from the published API categories rather than a downloadable OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: Field Medical
providers.description: Field Medical, Inc. is a Carlsbad, California clinical-stage cardiac electrophysiology company founded in 2022 by Dr. Steven Mickelsen to build a second-generation pulsed field ablation (PFA) platform. Its FieldForce Ablation System pairs a focal catheter design with proprietary FieldBending energy and is positioned as the first PFA system purpose-built for ventricular arrhythmia ablation, with atrial fibrillation applications in development. The company holds FDA Breakthrough Device Designation and a place in the FDA TAP Pilot Program for its VT indication, has published first-in-human VCAS data in Circulation, and has raised roughly $75M across Series A and Series B. Field Medical is a medical device manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no public REST/GraphQL API and no SDKs. Its only machine-readable public surface is the llms.txt and anonymous site MCP endpoint that its Wix-hosted corporate website serves.

providers.name: Telesair
providers.description: Telesair, Inc. is a Southern California MedTech company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in Irvine, California, that builds respiratory care hardware for patients with respiratory insufficiency. Its flagship product is Bonhawa, a purpose-built High Flow Oxygen Therapy (HFOT) respiratory humidifier that delivers warmed and humidified respiratory gases to spontaneously breathing pediatric and adult patients (10 kg and up) across a 2-80 L/min flow range, with separate pediatric and adult modes, a streamlined disinfection process and a touchscreen interface. Bonhawa holds both FDA 510(k) clearance (October 2023) and the CE Mark under the European Medical Device Regulation (August 2023), and is distributed to US hospitals under an exclusive agreement with Tri-anim Health Services. Telesair also supplies AVEA disposable expiratory filters. Telesair is a medical device manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract. Its only machine-readable agent surface is the Wix platform's Site Visitor Assistant MCP endpoint and an llms.txt served from its own marketing host.

providers.name: 28 labs
providers.description: 28labs Inc. operates She's Well (sheswell.co), a consumer fertility-care platform that bundles egg freezing, fertility testing, IVF coordination, clinic visits, labs, medications, and concierge nurse support into a single transparent subscription plan starting at $249/month over up to 60 months. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a business-to-consumer digital-health service with no public developer platform, API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Docquity
providers.description: Docquity is a Singapore-headquartered digital health company operating Asia's largest verified professional network for licensed healthcare practitioners, with more than 500,000 verified doctors across nine markets including Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore and Taiwan. Its flagship product, Dx, is an AI clinical thinking partner that bundles clinical search and decision support, accredited continuing medical education, peer community and case discussion, and patient-ready summary notes into an invite-only mobile and web platform gated behind medical-credential verification. For life-sciences and enterprise partners Docquity sells an Intelligence Suite comprising Pulse, which measures healthcare-professional conviction and engagement, and Dialog, which runs field engagement and activation programs against that audience. Docquity also operates Docquity Jobs, a medical recruitment board. The company publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable specification; its api.docquity.com backend and id.docquity.com identity service exist to serve its own first-party applications and are not offered to third-party developers.

providers.name: Gaia
providers.description: Gaia (Gaia Family) is a value-based family-building company that makes fertility treatment financially accessible. Founded by Nader AlSalim after his own multi-year IVF journey, Gaia replaces unpredictable cycle-by-cycle IVF billing with fixed-price, all-inclusive plans and monthly payments, backed by a protection model that offers more tries — or money back — if treatment does not succeed. It partners with 180+ fertility clinics across the US and UK, covering IVF, egg freezing, embryo transfer, hormone and lab testing, and fertility navigation, and also offers fertility benefits to employers. This profile is a company lead (no public API surface) maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: measureQuick
providers.description: measureQuick provides a residential HVAC commissioning platform that reads technician probes, scores systems against live conditions, and generates trusted reports. It supports over 80 tools across 17 brands, offering free and paid plans with advanced diagnostics, cloud dashboards, and training resources.

providers.name: Prenetics
providers.description: Prenetics Global Limited (NASDAQ: PRE) is a consumer healthcare and longevity company whose flagship brand is IM8, a science-backed daily-nutrition and longevity supplement line co-founded with David Beckham that reached roughly $120M in annual recurring revenue within its first year. The company's IM8 Health direct-to-consumer storefront runs on Shopify and exposes an agent-native commerce surface: it publishes an /llms.txt agent guide and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile at /.well-known/ucp that advertises a hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) shopping endpoint, letting AI agents search the catalog, build carts, and drive buyer-approved checkout via Shop Pay, Google Pay, and Shopify card handlers. Prenetics itself publishes no separate developer/API program; the agent-commerce surface is the IM8 Health UCP/MCP storefront.

providers.name: Rupa Health
providers.description: Rupa Health (now a Fullscript company) is a healthcare platform that lets functional and root-cause medicine practitioners order, track, and receive results from specialty and functional lab tests across hundreds of lab companies through a single unified dashboard. It provides a lab test catalog, patient result portals, practitioner ordering and billing, phlebotomy coordination, and educational resources (Rupa University, the Root Cause Medicine podcast, and a lab reference guide). Rupa integrates with a range of EHR/EMR systems used by independent practitioners but does not publish a public developer API or developer portal at this time. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Sevaro
providers.description: Sevaro (Sevaro Health) is a physician-led virtual neurology company that delivers telestroke, teleneurohospitalist rounding, remote EEG, neuro-intensive care, neuro-rehab and ambulatory neurology clinic services to hospitals across the United States. Its clinical delivery runs on Synapse AI, an integrated telemedicine platform that unifies EMR access, imaging, video, automated urgent call routing (Sevaro OneCall), AI stroke triage, ambient documentation and analytics, with companion Sevaro Video, Synapse for Providers, Synapse Analytics and Triage by Sevaro mobile surfaces. Sevaro sells to hospital systems through a demo-and-contract motion; it publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Sofia
providers.description: Sofía is a 100% Mexican digital health insurance company that modernizes traditional medical coverage for enterprises, individuals, and families. Its plans combine zero-deductible major and minor medical care, preventive care with an assigned primary-care physician, and unlimited no-cost video consultations, all managed through a mobile app and an HR administrative portal. Sofía operates its own integrated medical network (SofíaMed) of hospitals and specialists, offers add-ons such as maternity, mental health, dental, and international coverage, and reimburses claims in an average of five business days. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Sofía positions insurance as a digital-first, member-centric health experience rather than a paper policy.

providers.name: Sprinter Health
providers.description: Sprinter Health is an in-home preventive and diagnostic healthcare company that pairs trained community health workers ("Sprinters") who visit patients at home with a virtual team of physicians, nurses, and care navigators. Its hybrid Sprinter Care+ model delivers vitals, blood draws, ECGs, cancer and diabetic screenings, wellness visits, medication reconciliation, care-gap closure, health risk assessments, and social-needs screening, and partners with health plans such as Humana, Molina Healthcare, and Anthem. Backed by a16z, Accel, General Catalyst, and GV. No public developer or API surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's identity, security posture, and legal/trust properties.

providers.name: Brightline
providers.description: Brightline is an award-winning pediatric mental health practice delivering therapy, psychiatry (including medication management), and psychological testing for children and adolescents up to age 18, using an evidence-based, family-focused model that begins with a structured diagnostic evaluation. It treats anxiety, OCD, ADHD, disruptive behavioral disorders, depression, trauma, grief, and autism-spectrum symptoms via in-person clinics in New York and telehealth across NY, NJ, CT, MA, and WA, and operates BrightLife Kids, a free California state-funded behavioral health program for families with children up to age 12. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Threshold Ventures; Brightline is a consumer/clinical healthcare provider with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Evvy
providers.description: Evvy is a women's health company offering at-home vaginal microbiome testing and personalized care. Its CLIA-certified metagenomic (mNGS) Vaginal Health Test identifies over 700 bacteria and fungi from a self-collected sample, with results reviewed by licensed clinicians who deliver personalized insights and clinician-designed treatment programs for conditions such as bacterial vaginosis, aerobic vaginitis, yeast infections, recurrent UTIs, and fertility-related concerns. Evvy also sells a line of vaginal health products including probiotics and boric-acid, hyaluronic-acid, and probiotic suppositories, plus a provider program for clinicians and a large library of science-backed educational content. Backed by General Catalyst, Evvy was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Evvy is a direct-to-consumer health and e-commerce business and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Hormona
providers.description: Hormona is a women's hormonal-health company founded in 2020 by Karolina Lofqvist and Jasmine Tagesson, with offices in London, UK and Stockholm, Sweden. It builds a hormone-tracking mobile app together with an at-home hormone monitor and urine-test kits that users scan with a phone camera to get real-time, quantitative hormone results without a lab visit. The app uses AI to learn each user's patterns and predict when PMS or period symptoms are likely, offering 30+ tools to manage hormonal symptoms and supporting women from their first period through perimenopause and menopause. Hormona is distributed on the App Store and Google Play and is used by women in 185+ countries. It is a direct-to-consumer product with no public developer API program.

providers.name: LifeSite
providers.description: LifeSite is a data protection and digital asset company that helps organizations safeguard sensitive information, simplify compliance, and digitally verify ownership. Its Vault product is an encrypted store for personally identifiable, financial, and health information used by both enterprises and families to organize and collaborate on vital documents. TokenX, its Web3 arm, tokenizes real-world assets — critical minerals, carbon credits, and sports and consumer goods — so provenance and ownership can be authenticated without blockchain expertise. A Wellness product covers health, testing, and vaccination tracking for enterprises and events, and a Platform offering exposes LifeSite's building blocks and APIs for partners building tailored data-management applications. LifeSite is sales-led: the Platform APIs are described publicly but no developer portal, API reference, or specification is published, and access is arranged through a demo request.

providers.name: Novoic
providers.description: Novoic is a London-based clinical AI company building speech biomarkers for the early detection of Alzheimer's disease and cognitive impairment. Its technology analyzes how people speak - acoustic and linguistic patterns - to screen for subtle cognitive change in about ten minutes on any smart device. Products include Storyteller (automated, browser-based speech-based cognitive testing), Dashboard (an enterprise platform for running screening programs across sites with AI-assisted triage and analytics), and a Speech API for direct access to their speech processing, automated speech recognition, quality control, and speech-biomarker models. Novoic is deployed across 50+ medical institutions, partners with the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, and emphasizes HIPAA/GDPR compliance. It also publishes two open-source feature-extraction libraries, surfboard (audio) and blabla (linguistics).

providers.name: UptimeHealth
providers.description: UptimeHealth is a healthcare operations platform for managing medical equipment service, compliance documentation, and facility maintenance across dental, medical, and veterinary practices from a single dashboard. The platform tracks devices, automates compliance tasks and logs, and coordinates repair service requests, reporting 73,000+ devices protected across 6,000+ facilities. UptimeHealth publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation — its platform (uptimecontroller.com) is a closed SaaS application.

providers.name: Aidence
providers.description: Aidence is a radiology AI company founded in Amsterdam in 2015 that builds clinical AI for the lung cancer pathway. Its flagship product, Veye Lung Nodules (now DeepHealth Lung), is a CE-marked AI solution that detects, classifies, quantifies, and measures growth of pulmonary nodules on chest CT scans, and is the AI of choice in NHS England's Targeted Lung Health Checks screening programme. Aidence was acquired by RadNet in 2022 and now operates under the DeepHealth brand; aidence.com redirects to deephealth.com/aidence. The product integrates with hospital systems over DICOM/PACS via the Veye Engine rather than a public developer REST API — no public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published. This profile captures the company's identity plus its probed security and disclosure posture.

providers.name: Almanac Health
providers.description: Almanac Health is a clinical AI company building a research-validated clinical decision support platform, delivered as Almanac Chat, that brings specialist-grade, evidence-based answers to clinicians at the point of care. Founded by physician-researcher Cyril Zakka, MD, the platform is designed to work within existing electronic health record (EHR) workflows, is governed by institutional controls, and is grounded in peer-reviewed research rather than pharmaceutical promotion. In April 2026 the company raised a $10 million seed round led by F-Prime with participation from General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This API Evangelist profile currently tracks the company's public web, trust, and security surface; Almanac Health does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Benchmark Electronics
providers.description: Benchmark Electronics, Inc. is an advanced electronics engineering and manufacturing services (EMS) company headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. The company provides integrated design, engineering, and manufacturing services from prototypes to high-volume production, including procurement, logistics, and repair. Benchmark serves original equipment manufacturers in defense, medical technologies, commercial aerospace, industrial, next-gen communications, advanced computing, and semiconductor capital equipment markets. The company operates approximately 22 locations in 8 countries with around 13,000 employees.

providers.name: Walgreens Boots Alliance
providers.description: Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA) is a global pharmacy-led health and wellbeing enterprise operating in more than 25 countries, with pharmacy chains Walgreens in the US and Boots in the UK, pharmaceutical wholesale and distribution through Alliance Healthcare, and specialty pharmacy operations. WBA operates as a Fortune 100 company and global healthcare platform, leveraging data science, AI, and digital health technologies to serve patients, customers, and health systems. While WBA's primary developer APIs are offered through the Walgreens Developer Program, the enterprise also uses healthcare data platforms for population health management, specialty pharmacy integration, and digital health services.

providers.name: Zetagen Therapeutics
providers.description: Zetagen Therapeutics is a private, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2015 and based in Syracuse, New York, where it has operated from laboratory space in the Central New York Biotech Accelerator at SUNY Upstate Medical University since 2017. It develops locally administered small-molecule therapies for metastatic and primary cancers to bone and other organs, built on a proprietary "Zeta" platform derived from the company's discovery of a new molecular pathway acting through the Met5-enkephalin / opioid growth factor receptor signalling axis. Its oncology pipeline includes ZetaMet (Zeta-BC-003) for metastatic breast cancer to bone, which received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation in December 2021 and Health Canada authorisation for a Phase 2a study in January 2022 and reported Phase 2a results at ASCO in June 2026; ZetaMet-P (Zeta-PC-004) for prostate cancer; ZetaMAST (Zeta-MBC-005) for metastatic breast cancer in liver; Zeta-BC-007; and ZetaOnc. Its osteologic programme is ZetaFuse, a synthetic osteoinductive bone graft studied in anterior cervical discectomy and fusion. The company reached 64 worldwide patents in 2024, has been funded by NCI and NIAMS grants, a $5.34M Series A, a $9.79M Series B and an oversubscribed Series B1 closed in November 2025, and its shares trade on secondary markets. Zetagen Therapeutics runs no developer program and publishes no product API, developer portal or API documentation. The only machine-readable surface reachable without credentials is the WordPress REST content API behind zetagen.com, catalogued here.

providers.name: BrightInsight
providers.description: BrightInsight is a regulated digital health platform for biopharma and medtech. Its cloud-based, microservices platform captures, transmits and analyzes data from CE-marked and FDA-regulated medical devices, combination products, apps and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) in compliance with global security, privacy and regulatory requirements. The platform integrates with 400+ medical devices across 50+ manufacturers, connects to EHRs in 500+ U.S. provider networks, and is available in 48 countries. Founded in 2017 (formerly Flex Digital Health) and based in Alviso, California, BrightInsight is used by top biopharma and medtech companies to build and launch commercial regulated digital health solutions. It is a sales-led enterprise platform with no public developer portal or public API; integration is delivered under managed engagements.

providers.name: Illuminate Education
providers.description: Illuminate Education is a K-12 education technology company providing assessment, data analytics, and Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) tools to schools and districts. Its platform serves roughly 17 million students across 5,200 schools and districts in all 50 states, taking a "whole child" approach that combines academic and social-emotional-behavioral data. Marquee products are FastBridge (universal screening and progress monitoring), DnA (standards-based assessment creation and scoring), and eduCLIMBER (MTSS collaboration and district data management). Illuminate does not publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI; data exchange runs through education-interoperability standards (LTI 1.0/1.1 Certified, OneRoster, Ed-Fi 2.5+, QTI) and partner/SIS/LMS integrations. It is a portfolio company of Insight Partners, headquartered in Irvine, California.

providers.name: voize
providers.description: voize is a German healthcare AI company (voize GmbH) building a voice-documentation platform for long-term care, skilled nursing, and disability-support facilities. Caregivers speak naturally on a smartphone during patient care and voize's on-device and cloud speech models convert the free speech into structured, categorized entries that sync bi-directionally in real time into the facility's electronic health record (EHR) system. The product reduces documentation burden for nursing staff, works offline, recognizes patient names and corrects grammar, and integrates directly with major EHRs used in skilled nursing. voize is backed by HV Capital and operates in Germany and the United States. It ships a mobile application rather than a public developer API, but exposes EHR integrations, a trust center, and a vulnerability disclosure / bug bounty program on its public surface.

providers.name: IXL Learning
providers.description: IXL Learning is a K-12 personalized practice platform with 17,000+ skills across Math, Language Arts, Science, Social Studies, and Spanish, plus the IXL Real-Time Diagnostic and skill recommendations. IXL is sold primarily as a SaaS subscription to families, teachers, schools, and districts. Its integration surface is school-rostering and SSO, not a public developer API: IXL supports Clever (SSO + rostering), ClassLink (SSO + OneRoster auto-rostering), OneRoster CSV/REST, LTI, Google Classroom, and SAML SSO for district deployments. There is no public REST API portal, no published OpenAPI, and no partner developer program.

providers.name: AdaptX
providers.description: AdaptX is a Seattle-based clinical performance management company (founded 2016 as MDMetrix, renamed AdaptX in 2021) whose self-serve platform reads a hospital's existing electronic medical record data and turns it into near-real-time analytics that clinical, quality, operational and finance leaders use to measure and reduce clinical variation. Customers include Seattle Children's, Memorial Hermann, Children's Minnesota, USA Health and Kittitas Valley Healthcare, with published case studies covering surgical capacity, emergency department time-to-triage, length of stay, anesthetic greenhouse-gas reduction and health-equity stratification. The product is delivered as a hosted SaaS application on AWS to contracted health systems; as of this profiling pass AdaptX publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API description.

providers.name: Aledade
providers.description: Aledade is a physician-led public benefit corporation and national leader in value-based care, partnering with independent primary care practices, community health centers, and health systems. It pairs data analytics, guided clinical workflows, integrated care solutions, and payer contracts to help primary care organizations succeed in accountable care organizations (ACOs) and value-based payment models, improving patient outcomes while supporting the business sustainability of independent practices. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of gv, ivp, and lightspeed-venture-partners.

providers.name: BillionToOne
providers.description: BillionToOne is a molecular diagnostics company using proprietary single-molecule Quantitative Counting Template (QCT) technology to detect disease at the DNA level from cell-free DNA. Its Unity prenatal screening suite (Unity Complete, Unity Confirm, and Unity fetal antigen tests) delivers non-invasive prenatal testing from maternal blood at nine weeks, and its Northstar oncology line (Northstar Select and Northstar Response) provides liquid-biopsy therapy selection and real-time treatment-response monitoring. BillionToOne integrates with electronic medical records through a collaboration with Epic and delivers results through its provider and patient portals. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global, Norwest Venture Partners, and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Bold
providers.description: Bold (Age Bold, Inc.) is an AI-enabled healthy-aging company founded in 2019 by Amanda Rees and Hari Arul that combines age-friendly virtual care with senior-focused exercise and nutrition programs for Medicare members. The platform delivers personalized at-home programs — live and on-demand classes, balance and fall-prevention regimens, pain and mobility programs, nutrition coaching, and telehealth visits with clinicians — to adults 65 and older, distributed through Medicare Advantage plans, provider groups, and the CMS ACCESS program rather than sold as a developer platform. Bold reports its balance programs lower fall risk and its pain programs reduce joint pain among participating members, and states its platform is HIPAA compliant and requires no lengthy IT integration for plan partners. The company has raised roughly $27M, with a $17M Series A led by Rethink Impact alongside Andreessen Horowitz Bio + Health, Khosla Ventures, Samsung Next, GingerBread Capital, and Primetime Partners. As of this enrichment pass Bold publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or partner API surface — integrations are handled through its partnerships team.

providers.name: ConnectRN
providers.description: connectRN is a Waltham, Massachusetts based per-diem (PRN) healthcare staffing marketplace that connects nurses, CNAs and allied clinicians with open shifts at hospitals, home health and hospice agencies, and skilled nursing facilities across the United States. Clinicians browse and claim shifts through the connectRN mobile app with no minimum commitment, no required weekends or holidays, and same-day pay; facilities post shifts, auto-backfill open coverage and approve timesheets through a web platform at app.connectrn.com. In April 2026 connectRN merged with SnapCare, combining connectRN's PRN clinician community with SnapCare's Booker workforce technology platform. connectRN operates a public status page but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its API host api.connectrn.com serves the first-party mobile and web applications only.

providers.name: Grow Therapy
providers.description: Grow Therapy is a mental-health platform that connects individuals with licensed therapists and prescribers, offering virtual and in-person talk therapy plus medication management in one insurance-integrated experience. The company operates a two-sided marketplace: a client-facing product for finding, booking, and paying for care (with insurance verification and an average session cost around $21 for covered clients) and a provider portal that gives clinicians scheduling, billing, telehealth, and practice-management tooling. Grow also partners with employers, physicians, and payors on B2B mental-health access. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network; Grow Therapy publishes a public Statuspage but does not expose a public developer API, so this profile captures its company identity, operational transparency, and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Hello Heart
providers.description: Hello Heart is a digital health company that combines a mobile app, connected blood-pressure monitors, a smart pill box, and the Nia AI assistant (trained on ACC/AHA guidelines) to help people proactively manage cardiovascular health. Sold primarily to employers, health plans, unions, and public-sector benefits programs as a covered heart-health benefit, the platform pairs self-monitoring with clinically-grounded, "safe AI" coaching to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiac risk. Hello Heart is HITRUST CSF certified, SOC 2 Type 2 audited, NIST CSF aligned, and HIPAA compliant, with data encrypted in transit and at rest and stored within U.S. borders. It exposes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public identity, security, and compliance posture.

providers.name: Naluri
providers.description: Naluri is a digital health and corporate wellness platform operating across Southeast Asia. It delivers Employee Assistance Programmes, chronic disease management (mental health, obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and cholesterol), health coaching and consultations, performance workshops, and Mental Health First Aid training for employers, insurers, and individuals. The company reports serving over one million members and 200-plus companies, and states it is certified for HIPAA, GDPR, and ISO/IEC 27001. No public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Ophelia Health
providers.description: Ophelia is a telehealth company providing private, evidence-based medication-assisted treatment (MAT) for opioid use disorder from home. Founded in 2019 by Zack Gray and Mattan Griffel and headquartered in New York City, Ophelia connects patients with licensed clinicians for video visits, prescribes Suboxone (buprenorphine + naloxone) sent to a local pharmacy, and provides ongoing care-team support seven days a week. The subscription service accepts most major insurance plans, including Medicaid, and is licensed to provide care across 49 states and Washington, D.C. Ophelia is a direct-to-consumer clinical service and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner API program; this profile captures its public web presence and domain security posture.

providers.name: Physiohome
providers.description: Physiohome, operating as Ameen (رعاية أمين), is a Saudi Arabia-based, tech-enabled provider of home rehabilitation and physical therapy services. Founded in 2021 out of a Ministry of Health sector accelerator, the company delivers physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, nutritional therapy, and personal training for adults and seniors in patients' homes and rehabilitation centers. Its platform manages the full care journey from assessment and treatment planning through session tracking, provider equipping, and reporting, with 100+ active service providers operating across nine cities and a wider network of 700+ providers. Ameen offers iOS and Android apps, an online booking flow, and a patient portal, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. It is a portfolio company of Sanabil 500 (500 Global) and Saudi Venture Capital.

providers.name: Radical Health
providers.description: Radical Health is a Khosla Ventures-backed healthcare AI company that produces personalized, expert-reviewed cancer treatment reports for patients in the United States. Its platform ingests a patient's medical records and synthesizes oncology research, clinical trials, and prior patient outcomes into a tailored report within days, drawing on 5.3 million research papers, 11.8 million patient journeys, 20,000 treatment options, and 48,800+ active US clinical trials. The service pairs an always-on AI nurse navigator ("Alice") with human oncology oversight from institutions including UCLA, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, and Kaiser Permanente, and connects to 70,000+ US healthcare institutions (Epic, Kaiser, Ascension, HCA, Medicare) for records access. Reports are informational and educational only, not medical advice. Radical Health is HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II certified and operates as a consumer subscription product ($110/month with a 7-day free trial); it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Regard
providers.description: Regard is an AI-powered clinical diagnosis and documentation platform for hospitals and health systems. It reviews 100% of a patient's electronic health record (EHR) to surface and recommend evidence-supported diagnoses, then generates clinical documentation at the point of care. Regard positions itself around "earning revenue through better care, not queries," spanning clinical notes, mid-revenue-cycle denial prevention and revenue capture, HCC risk-adjustment capture, and screening for care gaps. The company reports 12.9M+ recommended diagnoses accepted by clinicians and $50M+ in revenue generated for health systems. Regard integrates directly with EHRs rather than exposing a public developer API; its Health IT Module is ONC 2015 Cures Update certified. Backed by Foundry Group and Techstars. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Seer
providers.description: Seer, Inc. (NASDAQ: SEER) is a Redwood City, California life-sciences company pioneering proteomics, the large-scale study of proteins. Its Proteograph Product Suite pairs engineered nanoparticles with automated sample preparation and mass spectrometry to profile tens of thousands of proteins across biological samples at scale, and its cloud-based Proteograph Analysis System (PAS) software processes and interprets the resulting proteomic data for pharmaceutical, biopharma, and academic research. Seer exposes no public developer API; its software surface is the login-gated PAS platform delivered to customers of the Proteograph suite.

providers.name: Actium Health
providers.description: ActiumHealth is the conversational AI platform for healthcare patient communication, operated as a division of Syllable Corporation. Its voice, SMS, chat and email agents automate inbound and outbound patient calls across appointment scheduling, prescription refill, call routing, referral management, patient surveys, care coordination and revenue cycle workflows for health systems, patient access centers, healthcare contact centers and practice groups, with more than 70 million calls reported handled. The agents integrate with Epic, Cerner and Meditech EHRs through those vendors' APIs, and the platform is marketed as built to SOC 2, HITRUST and HIPAA standards. ActiumHealth consumes EHR APIs rather than publishing one and runs no developer program on actiumhealth.com; the underlying agentic platform API, SDKs, CLI, MCP server and documentation are published by its parent at syllable.ai and catalogued here as `syllable`.

providers.name: HealthEngine
providers.description: HealthEngine is Australia's largest consumer healthcare marketplace and patient-engagement platform, founded in 2006 and headquartered in Perth, Western Australia. Its consumer app and website let millions of Australians search a national directory of primary-care providers and book, manage, and attend appointments (including telehealth) across GP, dental, allied-health, and specialist practices. For practices, HealthEngine sells a SaaS suite - GP Complete, Patient Connect, Online Booking, Appointment Reminders and Recalls, Featured Listings, online payments, patient reviews, and Scripts - that plugs into the practice's existing software. It maintains private, real-time integrations into 25+ Australian practice management systems (Best Practice / Bp Premier, MedicalDirector Pracsoft, Zedmed, Cliniko, Genie, Gentu, Medtech, Nookal, PracSuite, Dental4Windows, and others) so appointment availability and bookings sync directly with the front desk. Home market is Australia. HealthEngine does NOT publish a public developer portal, REST OpenAPI, or HL7 FHIR endpoint - its API surface is a set of gated, partner-only PMS integrations rather than a self-serve developer program, so this profile is an honest identity stub with no public machine-readable contract to harvest.

providers.name: Irhythmtech
providers.description: iRhythm Technologies is a publicly traded (NASDAQ: IRTC) digital healthcare company specializing in ambulatory cardiac monitoring for the detection and management of heart arrhythmias. Its Zio service pairs a wearable single-lead ECG biosensor patch (Zio monitor and Zio AT) with FDA-cleared AI/deep-learning algorithms, qualified cardiac technician verification, and cloud-based data analytics to produce end-of-wear diagnostic reports for clinicians. The platform includes the ZioSuite clinician portal for report interpretation and patient management, the MyZio patient app for symptom logging and education, EHR integration, and telehealth workflows. iRhythm was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It does not publish a public developer API or documentation portal; enrichment is limited to public identity, trust, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Pluto
providers.description: Pluto (Pluto Health, trypluto.com now pluto.health) is an AI-powered clinical intelligence and care-delivery platform that unifies fragmented health data from roughly 90% of US health systems. It aggregates medical records, insurance data, and social determinants of health, then applies AI-driven clinical intelligence to surface care gaps, coordinate preventive care, screenings, vaccines and at-home lab testing, and match patients to clinical trials. Pluto offers turnkey, white-label, or API-based deployment of its clinical operations. It is backed by Sierra Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: TMRW Life Sciences *
providers.description: TMRW Life Sciences is a medical technology company that builds the world's first and only FDA-cleared automated platform for the safe management and storage of frozen eggs and embryos used in IVF and fertility treatment. Its cryo-storage hardware combines robotic specimen handling with digital tracking, chain-of-custody monitoring, and real-time visibility for fertility clinics and their patients, replacing manual, paper-based handling of irreplaceable reproductive tissue. Deployed at clinic networks including CCRM Fertility, Pinnacle Fertility, RFC, and IVIRMA North America. TMRW is a private company backed by GV (Google Ventures). It publishes a Security & Trust program (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27018) but does not expose a public developer portal, API, or specification surface.

providers.name: ExaCare AI
providers.description: ExaCare AI is a post-acute and senior care operations platform that applies AI to admissions, referral management, prior authorization, and reimbursement workflows across skilled nursing, home health, hospice, and assisted living providers. It reads inbound referral and admissions packets, extracts clinical and payer data, and automates the back-office work of accepting and reimbursing patients, with integrations into referral platforms, hospital systems, and EHRs. ExaCare is a private company backed by Insight Partners; it ships a customer web application and a Vanta-hosted Trust Center (HIPAA) but publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Faks
providers.description: Faks is a French SaaS platform that digitizes and streamlines the commercial relationships across the pharmacy ecosystem. It gives pharmacies, pharmacy groups (groupements), and laboratories a single place to manage supplier relationships, commercial claims and disputes (litiges), expired and returnable product handling, promotions, and sell-in / sell-out performance. Faks connects to pharmacy management systems (LGO), purchasing platforms, and accounting tools through its Konnect integrations to automate what has traditionally been manual, paper, and email-driven work between the ~18,000 pharmacies, ~100 groups, and ~500 laboratories it targets in France. The company is backed by Seedcamp. Faks does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and the enrichment surfaces that could be probed.

providers.name: Heard
providers.description: Heard (Heard Technologies, Inc.) is the financial management platform built specifically for therapists and wellness practitioners in private practice. Founded in 2019 and based in Seattle, Washington, Heard pairs easy-to-use software with a dedicated human team to handle bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and business banking in a single subscription, so licensed mental health and allied health clinicians can focus on their clients. Heard serves solo and single-owner group practices across the United States, from newer sole proprietors to established S corporations, and connects with tools practices already use such as SimplePractice, TherapyNotes, Headway, Jane App, Stripe, and Square. Heard exposes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures the company identity, its public web properties, and the published llms.txt.

providers.name: medigami-com
providers.description: Medigami is a health technology company focused on providing innovative medical imaging solutions and data analytics platforms for healthcare providers. The company offers a suite of APIs that enable integration of imaging data, patient records, and analytics dashboards, facilitating streamlined workflows and improved diagnostic accuracy. Medigami’s services aim to enhance interoperability across radiology systems, support AI-driven image analysis, and deliver secure, compliant data exchange for hospitals and clinics.

providers.name: Tia
providers.description: Tia is a women's healthcare company that operates in-person clinics and a virtual care platform, bringing primary care, gynecology, mental health, and wellness services into one connected care experience. Founded in 2017 and backed by Canaan Partners, Tia runs clinics in New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix, offers virtual visits across multiple states, and partners with health systems. Tia is a consumer healthcare provider and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Backpack Healthcare
providers.description: Backpack Healthcare is a virtual (telehealth) pediatric and family mental health provider delivering therapy, psychiatry, and medication management for children, tweens, teens, young adults, and adults. It offers age-based care (Littles 4-10, Tweens & Teens 11-17, Young Adults 18+, and Adults) across concerns including ADHD, anxiety, autism spectrum disorder, depression, OCD, maternal mental health, and substance use, alongside a consumer Self Care / Care Companion mobile app. Backpack partners with health plans, schools, health systems, and community and government agencies to expand access to youth behavioral health, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Cala Health
providers.description: Cala Health is a bioelectronic medicine company that develops wearable neuromodulation therapies for chronic disease. Its FDA-cleared Cala kIQ and Cala TRIO systems deliver TAPS (Transcutaneous Afferent Patterned Stimulation) therapy through a wrist-worn device that is physician-prescribed and clinically proven to reduce action hand tremors associated with essential tremor and Parkinson's disease. Patients manage therapy and view results through the MyCala portal, and clinicians access data through the Cala 360 provider portal. Cala Health is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company operating in the life-sciences / medical-device sector. This profile currently exposes no public developer API; enrichment has captured the company's public security, privacy, and support surface.

providers.name: Calibrate
providers.description: Calibrate is a telehealth metabolic-health and weight-loss company that pairs clinician-prescribed GLP-1 medications with 1:1 video coaching and a science-backed educational curriculum to help members improve metabolic health and achieve sustainable weight loss. Programs are sold directly to individuals (from $199/month) and through employer benefits. Calibrate delivers its service through consumer web and iOS mobile apps rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks the company's public web and account surface. Backed by Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: Carepatron
providers.description: Carepatron is a cloud-based healthcare practice management and EHR platform for therapists, counselors, psychologists, health coaches, nutritionists, and other practitioners. It brings client records, appointment scheduling and online booking, telehealth, AI-assisted clinical notes and documentation, and billing/invoicing with insurance claims into one workspace, and markets HIPAA/SOC/GDPR compliance across 100,000+ clinicians in 120+ countries. As of this review Carepatron does NOT publish a documented public developer API - its pricing page lists "API (coming soon)" on the Advanced plan, and there is no developer portal, API reference, published base URL, OpenAPI definition, or SDK. Third-party connectivity today is limited to a handful of native integrations (Zoom, accounting software, Google Tag Manager). The APIs listed below are logical/product-area groupings modeled from Carepatron's own feature set; their endpoints are NOT documented and are marked as modeled, not confirmed.

providers.name: Meditopia
providers.description: Meditopia is a holistic mental-wellbeing platform founded in 2017 that blends psychology, technology, and wellness to support the mental, emotional, and physical health of individuals and organizations. For consumers it ships a meditation and mindfulness mobile app (sleep programs, guided meditations, personalized assessments, self-guided content) available in nine-plus languages and used by 40+ million people across 60 countries. For organizations it offers Meditopia for Work: a modern Employee Assistance Program (EAP), 1-on-1 expert sessions, a WellnessPass benefits platform, online trainings, and Soul, an AI wellbeing coach. Meditopia is backed by Creandum. The company operates a consumer mobile app and a B2B web platform; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Pear Suite
providers.description: Pear Suite is a care management platform built for community health workers, care navigators, doulas, and community-based organizations, describing itself as an operating system for community-based work. The platform provides custom assessments and care pathways, goal and outcome tracking, patient communication over phone, SMS, and encrypted email, client and population-level analytics, and billing and claims integration, connecting community health initiatives with health plans and health systems. Pear Suite reports serving 2,500+ community workers across 300+ organizations nationwide.

providers.name: Roger
providers.description: Roger (operated by Sanos Services GmbH, Berlin, Germany) is a B2B SaaS practice-management platform for dental clinics. It layers automation and AI onto existing German dental practice-management systems (PVS) such as CGM Z1, Charly, Dampsoft, Evident and Dento Office, adding patient recall, digital intake forms, WhatsApp/SMS communication, AI-assisted documentation with billing-position capture, digital treatment-plan signing, factoring with default protection and instant payout, and outsourced ZMV/reception staffing. The product is DSGVO/GDPR-compliant and hosted in Germany. As surfaced in the API Evangelist network via VC-portfolio discovery, Roger publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Spill
providers.description: Spill is a UK-based employee assistance programme (EAP) that delivers mental health support to employees directly inside the tools teams already use, such as Slack and Microsoft Teams. The platform offers same-day, message-based counselling, structured multi-session therapy courses for specific mental health conditions, drop-in group sessions, manager mental-health training, and self-guided wellbeing content, all through a single subscription. Spill serves over 600 companies on month-to-month terms and is backed by Seedcamp. It is a B2B software-as-a-service wellbeing product rather than an API provider; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been published.

providers.name: Terapify
providers.description: Terapify is an online therapy platform for the Spanish-speaking market, connecting individuals in Mexico and Latin America with certified psychologists for private, secure video-call sessions. Founded in 2019 and backed by 500 Global and Y Combinator, the platform matches patients to therapists via a therapeutic-affinity test, offers individual and couples therapy, parent orientation, and workplace mental-health programs for companies, plus mindfulness, yoga, and breathing resources. It operates as a consumer web and mobile (iOS/Android) product and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Apricot
providers.description: Apricot is an AI-native clinical documentation platform for home health and post-acute care agencies, founded by home-health operator Trent Smith and headquartered in Oklahoma. Its software cuts start-of-care (SOC) and OASIS documentation time by up to 85% and QA time by up to 40%, automating medication reconciliation, wound documentation, ICD coding recommendations, and narrative generation while capturing vitals, photos, signatures, and voice notes in the home and syncing to each agency's EMR configuration. Apricot is HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant and raised a Series A led by Insight Partners in 2025. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public web presence; Apricot currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Dental Monitoring
providers.description: Dental Monitoring provides AI-powered dental monitoring solutions that enable remote orthodontic care, allowing clinicians to track patient progress through a patented scanning device and cloud platform. The company offers a suite of tools for dentists and orthodontists to monitor treatment, engage patients, and integrate data into practice workflows, supporting multiple languages and regulatory compliance.

providers.name: FitOn
providers.description: FitOn is a consumer digital fitness and wellness platform offering free, on-demand workout classes (cardio, strength, yoga, Pilates, HIIT), guided meditation, personalized meal plans and nutrition tracking, recipes, and social challenges. FitOn serves 15 million+ members with celebrity and world-class trainers across mobile, web, and connected-TV apps (Apple TV, Roku, Chromecast, Fire TV). Its FitOn Health arm delivers an enterprise wellness benefit to employers, health plans, and brokers. FitOn is backed by Accel. As of this enrichment pass FitOn publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI; consumer and B2B integration is handled through partnership programs rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: GetHarley
providers.description: GetHarley is a UK-based telehealth and skincare platform delivering personalised, medical-grade skincare through online consultations. Patients answer questions about their skin concerns, book a video consultation, and are matched with one of a network of over 1,000 licensed dermatologists, aesthetic doctors, and plastic surgeons, who recommend a tailored regimen of medical-grade products delivered to the patient. GetHarley operates both a patient-facing storefront and a practitioner platform used by clinicians to manage recommendations, orders, and client relationships. Backed by Index Ventures, the company addresses concerns such as acne, fine lines, pigmentation, and ageing. As of this profile, GetHarley does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or an MCP server; this record captures its identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Octave Bioscience
providers.description: Octave Bioscience is a precision neurology company founded in 2014 and headquartered in Menlo Park, California, that develops blood-based multi-protein biomarker tests for chronic neurological disease. Its commercially available Octave Multiple Sclerosis Disease Activity (MSDA) Test measures a panel of serum proteins to produce a quantitative disease activity score used alongside clinical and imaging assessment, and is available across the United States through a strategic collaboration with Quest Diagnostics. The company is also developing a Multiple Sclerosis Disease Progression (MSDP) test and a Parkinson's disease biomarker assay supported by a Michael J. Fox Foundation grant. Octave publishes a public trust center documenting HITRUST, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, HIPAA and GDPR posture, but operates no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: ScreenPoint Medical
providers.description: ScreenPoint Medical is a Netherlands-based healthcare AI company, founded in 2014 by Professor Nico Karssemeijer and Professor Sir Michael Brady, that develops Transpara Breast AI for earlier detection of breast cancer in 2D (FFDM) and 3D (DBT) mammography. Transpara is vendor-agnostic, integrates into PACS and reading workflows via medical-imaging (DICOM) pipelines rather than a public developer API, and is FDA cleared (K241831, K232096) and CE marked (0344). The product is used in over 200 clinics across 25+ countries and is backed by three randomized controlled trials (including MASAI in The Lancet). The company is backed by Insight Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline: no public developer/API surface exists, but real security-disclosure and compliance posture were captured.

providers.name: Collective Medical
providers.description: Collective Medical is a full-continuum, real-time care collaboration network for healthcare, connecting hospitals, health systems, post-acute providers, health plans, and payers so care teams can coordinate around complex, high-risk, and vulnerable patients across the entire patient journey. Founded in Utah and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Kleiner Perkins, the platform is known for its real-time event notifications, ADT-based care-coordination alerts, and shared clinical insights used by emergency departments and care-management teams. Collective Medical was acquired by PointClickCare in 2020 and is now fully integrated into PointClickCare; its former developer, login, support, and legal surfaces are served through PointClickCare properties (developer.pointclickcare.com and pointclickcare.com). This profile tracks the Collective Medical brand within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hippocratic AI
providers.description: Hippocratic AI builds safety-focused generative AI agents for non-diagnostic healthcare tasks, powered by its Polaris constellation architecture. Polaris 5.0 is a multi-trillion-parameter constellation of specialized models clinically validated by U.S.-licensed clinicians. Hippocratic AI sells agents such as Nurse Co-Pilot and AI Front Door to health systems, payors, and life-sciences organizations through enterprise sales rather than a self-service public API.

providers.name: LabDoor
providers.description: Labdoor is an independent San Francisco-based supplement testing company that buys top-selling vitamins, supplements, protein powders and energy drinks off retail shelves and online stores and sends samples to FDA-registered analytical laboratories for chemical analysis of active ingredients and potential contaminants. It grades every product on Label Accuracy, Product Purity, Nutritional Value, Ingredient Safety and Projected Efficacy, then publishes the resulting rankings, scores and expert reports for free so consumers can compare products, and it funds that testing through retail sales and through Labdoor Enterprise certification and custom-testing services sold to manufacturers. Labdoor publishes no public developer API, SDKs, developer portal or API documentation as of July 2026.

providers.name: Pearly
providers.description: Pearly provides dental practice billing and revenue cycle management automation software. Its platform streamlines patient billing, accounts receivable, payment plans, letter automation, and integrates with practice management systems. Pearly serves DSOs, group practices, and private dental offices, offering online payments, reporting, and AI‑driven insights to improve cash flow and reduce administrative overhead.

providers.name: Aiwyn
providers.description: Aiwyn is a practice-automation platform built for modern accounting and CPA firms, unifying payments, practice management, client experience, and tax into a single relationship-centered system. Aiwyn Payments automates invoicing, card and ACH collection, and reconciliation; Aiwyn Practice covers time, billing, project management and resource planning; Aiwyn Experience delivers a unified client portal for engagement letters and secure document exchange; and Aiwyn Tax adds AI-assisted tax preparation. The company serves 800+ firms and raised $113M from KKR and Bessemer Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer portfolio company; Aiwyn publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface at this time, so enrichment is limited to identity, its published llms.txt, and probed domain security.

providers.name: Bhaptics
providers.description: Bhaptics creates advanced haptic technology, offering wearable haptic suits, vests, and accessories that enable developers to integrate tactile feedback into games, VR experiences, and other interactive applications. Their platform provides SDKs, APIs, and developer tools to control haptic patterns, synchronize with audio and visual cues, and deliver immersive sensations across a range of devices.

providers.name: Cortico
providers.description: Cortico (Cortico Health Technologies) is a Vancouver, British Columbia based healthcare connection platform, founded in 2019, that links patients, medical clinics, and health records across Canada and the United States. Its patient-engagement suite layers online booking, automated appointment reminders, secure two-way patient messaging, digital intake forms, telemedicine, specialist e-referrals, payments, and AI-driven administrative automation on top of the electronic medical records (EMRs) clinics already run — most notably a supported two-way integration with OSCAR EMR through that system's REST/SOAP web services, plus SMART on FHIR contextual launch and robotic process automation (RPA). Cortico is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified and compliant with HIPAA, PIPEDA, and PHIPA. Cortico consumes EMR and FHIR interfaces rather than publishing its own public developer API: as of this review there is no public developer portal, API reference, or FHIR CapabilityStatement, and integration is delivered through a partnership and onboarding model rather than self-serve API access.

providers.name: Everself
providers.description: Bariendo Inc. (now operating as Everself) is a science-forward digital health company pioneering non-surgical, endoscopic weight-loss care. Founded in 2023 by Harvard Medical School physicians Dr. Christopher C. Thompson (the inventor of Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty) and Dr. Pichamol Jirapinyo, the company delivers minimally invasive procedures — ESG Stomach Tightening, gastric balloon, and revision of prior bariatric surgery — alongside weight-loss medication and a 12-month concierge care program. Its consumer platform streamlines access to these interventions across a dozen-plus U.S. locations, with financing, telehealth consultations, and ongoing weight tracking. Bariendo/Everself is a consumer and clinical health service; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Foresight Diagnostics
providers.description: Foresight Diagnostics is a CLIA-certified, CAP-accredited cancer diagnostics company founded in 2020 in Boulder, Colorado by Stanford physicians and scientists, and since February 2026 a wholly owned subsidiary of Natera. Its Foresight CLARITY minimal residual disease (MRD) platform is a liquid-biopsy test powered by proprietary PhasED-Seq phased-variant sequencing and bioinformatics, detecting circulating tumor DNA at an analytical sensitivity below one part per million across lymphoma, lung and other solid tumors. The company sells laboratory testing services to biopharma sponsors, academic researchers and clinicians rather than software: it operates a central laboratory and publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Freed
providers.description: Freed is a San Francisco-based AI medical scribe and clinician assistant designed to reduce the documentation burden on healthcare providers. The product listens to patient visits and generates SOAP-style clinical notes, visit summaries, patient instructions, referral letters, and ICD-10 / CPT coding suggestions, then transfers the finalized note into the clinician's EHR via a browser-resident agent. Freed was founded in 2023 by former Facebook engineers Erez Druk (CEO) and Andrey Bannikov (CTO) after Druk's wife, a practicing family physician, experienced the daily toll of manual charting. The company is consumer self-serve: clinicians sign up for a 7-day free trial and then a monthly Starter, Core, Premier, or custom Groups plan with no enterprise sales required. As of 2025 Freed reported more than 20,000 paying clinician users and raised a $30M Series A led by Sequoia Capital, bringing total funding to $34M. The platform is HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified, and HITECH-ready; patient recordings are not stored.
